jobs.title: Graduate Internship, Operations Team
jobs.description:
About Ember

We're building the future of public transport — convenient, connected, affordable and zero-emission. Our goal is to make it easier to get from A to B with Ember than it is with your own car.

We’ve already demonstrated that it's possible to use electric buses more intensively than anyone else in the world. This leads to a massive emissions reduction and is only possible because we control the full-stack and integrate it tightly together. That includes the tech platform, the charging infrastructure and the vehicles themselves. This also means we’re providing a much better passenger experience with innovative features like demand-responsive stops.


We’ve come a long way and there’s much more to come, with the arrival of new vehicles, launch of new routes and hubs to continue to grow our network, it’s a very exciting time for Ember. The challenge is to scale 100x whilst staying lean, increasing efficiency and delivering an even better product experience. We’ve already successfully raised equity from some of Europe’s leading climate VCs and secured a large debt facility from our ethical banking partner, so we’re looking to build a team that can help us take things to the next level.


The role

This role is all about learning through doing, joining an existing team that takes care of day to day Operations. In the first instance, we're looking for generalist Interns who are keen to get to grips with all aspects of the Operational side of the business.


Sometimes that will mean troubleshooting, but after every fire you'll take a step back and think about how to help the team design and implement a process that could have dealt with the issue proactively.


What you will do

We're still very much a scale-up, so your role will be broad. At a minimum it will include:

  • Day to day involvement in vehicle, driver and route management

  • Looking after our customers across multiple channels

  • Helping to manage vehicle and charger maintenance

  • Assisting with the planning of future routes and expansion

You'll be engaging with a committed Operations team to ensure we have 24/7 coverage. Part of this may mean pitching in and helping with weekend or evening cover in case of incidents, whilst also working to ensure we keep these unanticipated events to a minimum.

Please note - this is an on-site role, and interested parties should only apply if they are able to work from our office in central Edinburgh.


Start dates and timings
We're looking to engage the right applicants for an initial period of three months, starting in October 2026


The long term
We're growing very rapidly, and our hope is very much that our internship programme could lead to permanent roles for the right candidates.


Diversity and equality

At Ember, we support diversity across our team and customers. We work to ensure every employee feels respected and able to give their best, whether temporary, part-time or full-time. We’re happy to offer flexible working patterns where they make sense, are compassionate when it comes to time off and offer enhanced maternity and paternity leave.

Read more about our approach in our Equal Opportunities Policy.


What’s on offer

This is a paid graduate internship, and conditions will satisfy the requirements of the National Living Wage.


How do I apply?

Apply using the form, providing a CV and a cover letter explaining why you're right for this opportunity. 


How you work and think is much more important to us than any specific industry experience. A genuine passion for climate or public transport, or even both, are also very valuable at an entry level, and we'll teach you the rest. You don't need to be a master of anything but shouldn't feel out of your depth anywhere.


Whether you're a university leaver or a veteran, a recent graduate looking for first-hand experience in Climate and Technology or a frustrated Public Transport enthusiast who would love to make the switch into this industry, we're keen to meet people with a passion to make a real difference.


We look for a range of qualities in all members of Ember's Operations Team, and the following should resonate with you:

  • A strong sense of what good really looks like whatever the topic, problem, or issue. After all, good is good.

  • An instinct and curiosity that draws you to problems and drives you to find a solution, rather than hoping someone else picks it up.

  • An innate structured thinker – everything is a series of steps which can be broken down and rationalised.

  • An ability to build strong relationships with a diverse range of people, from drivers to software developers.

We launched in October 2020 and are now running multiple routes across Scotland – including Dundee to Glasgow, Aberdeen to Edinburgh and connections from Glasgow and Edinburgh up to the west coast.  Other destinations across Scotland will follow in 2026 and 2027.

We're looking for the very best and most eager drivers to join the Ember team. Whether you have a passion for electric vehicles or simply for great customer service, we'd love to hear from you. It’s really important to us that we find people who are truly motivated to be a key part of a company that is proving that things can be done differently.


That means that for the right people, we’re happy to discuss relocation packages to various destinations across Scotland. Right now, that could mean locations such as:

  • Skye

  • Inverness

  • Oban

  • Fort William

We're a fast growing company with a track record of success, so this is an exciting time to join the future of public transport!


Responsibilities

As a driver, you're on the front-line. Not only will you be responsible for keeping the coach moving, you'll also provide on the ground operational support, which means having outstanding communication and organisational skills, proactivity to solve problems when there are delays and acting as the main point of contact for customers if they have any issues or need help. When things on the roads get busy, you'll be thinking one step ahead and will be working super closely with our Operations team to make sure that Ember's commitment to quality is always met.

This is a role for someone who is already at the top of their game as a driver but who is also looking for more responsibility and variety in their day to day. We're looking for forward-thinking drivers who can provide flexibility, and for the right individual there may be opportunities to be involved in the launch of a brand new hub including supporting new drivers coming on board by getting in early.

You should enjoy working with people and take pride in doing what it takes to deliver a great experience (as well as driving of course). That might mean helping someone with their bags, keeping the coach spick and span or making an effort to say a cheery 'hello' when people board.

We've built lots of new technology to help ensure customers get the best experience possible. That means you'll need to be open to learning new systems and using them in the correct way.

As a small business, we put a lot of trust into our drivers. We expect you to take pride in the work that you do and this will involve light cleaning duties throughout the day to keep our coaches in top condition. We are also evolving fast, so love people that want to give input into how we can do things better and who do this in a thoughtful, constructive way.


Benefits

  • £16.50 per hour starting rate.

  • £17.30 per hour after one year - we reward those who want to make a long term career.

  • £17.90 per hour if you become an Ember Ambassador - those who really live our values and give the best passenger experience.

  • Relief contracts are also available - £18.49 per hour (£16.50 base rate plus additional pay in lieu of holiday)

  • Overtime rates starting at £19.80 per hour.

  • Free CPC renewal for full time and part time drivers

  • 28 days paid annual holiday pro rata

  • Flexible annual leave - request your own holiday dates rather than being assigned them

  • Up to 10 days unpaid annual leave pro rata

  • 20 days paid leave for sickness, jury duty, parental or other unplanned leave pro rata

  • Established progression paths at a fast-growing company

  • Referral scheme - get paid for referring other top drivers to us

  • Friendly culture

  • You'll be driving a state-of-the-art electric coach

  • You’ll contribute to a hugely positive environmental impact, with every journey reducing emissions and traffic

Hours

We're running a 24/7 service, seven days per week, and looking for drivers wanting to work a variety of shifts. We'll give you five weeks’ notice of what the rota looks like so you have plenty of time to plan. We also frequently have overtime opportunities available at shorter notice.


Next Steps

Get in touch if you think you might be the right fit or learn more about Ember at www.ember.to


Requirements

You will need to meet these basic requirements:

  • Full PCV licence: Category D as a minimum

  • Up to date CPC and a digital tachograph card (or able to get both quickly)

  • Able to demonstrate high-quality driving, including smooth braking and a commitment to safety

  • Flexibility to work early, late or night shifts on any day of the week. In return, we'll try to make these as sociable as possible and agree them well in advance

jobs.title: Network Analyst - Senior
jobs.description:
We're looking for an experienced analyst to help design and grow Ember's network. You'll find route opportunities, build the timetables that run them, and use data to make every part of the network work better. We care less about which industry you've worked in than about your ability to think clearly, work in the real world as well as in code, and run several things at once to a high standard.

About Ember

We're building the future of public transport — convenient, affordable, connected and zero-emission. Our goal is to make it easier and more enjoyable to get from A to B with Ember than it is with your own car.

Ember is a tech company, not a traditional bus operator. We've built a platform that coordinates our entire operation – everything from monitoring vehicles and controlling chargers to selling tickets and calculating ETAs. This allows us to use electric buses more intensively than anyone else in the world, leading to a massive reduction in emissions. It also helps us provide a much better passenger experience, with innovative features like demand-responsive stops.

We’re still tiny, with a handful of routes and 98 buses. The challenge is to scale this 50x whilst staying lean, increasing efficiency and delivering an even better product experience. We’ve recently raised a Series A from some of Europe’s leading climate VCs and are looking for mission-driven individuals who want to get on board and help take us to the next level.

The role

This is a broad, hands-on role where you'll work across the full lifecycle of a route — from spotting an opportunity on a map to launching it, then making it better once it's running. We're a small team with a lot of ownership on offer. You'll decide what needs figuring out, and figure it out.

Finding new routes means going deep on Google Maps, researching existing transport alternatives, getting out into the real world to test ideas, and engaging with local communities to understand what they actually need. You'll need to know what's possible with our fleet of electric coaches and charging infrastructure, and to be comfortable trading off the most attractive-looking route design against the efficient use of those assets. The best route on paper isn't always the best route to run.

You'll also be one of the people shaping where Ember goes next. That means thinking about the network in the medium to long term rather than just individual routes, and being a strong voice in strategy conversations with the founders.

We don't build traditional clock-face timetables that ignore traffic patterns. Ours are probabilistic, accounting for how the use of each stop varies across days, weeks and seasons. You'll design them, take them through council consultation and registration with the Traffic Commissioner, and make sure the resulting service information ends up in the right places — everywhere from Google Maps to the paper timetables in bus shelters.

A great timetable is only the start. You'll work alongside our operations and charging teams to make sure we've hired and trained the right number of drivers, that there are decent rest facilities where they can take breaks, that we have enough vehicles to run the route, and that the charging will be there when it's needed. You won't do any of these things yourself — but you'll be central to figuring out what's needed and communicating that to other teams.

Launching a route is also only the start. Once a service is live, you'll use our data to assess how it's performing and work out how to make it better — sometimes a tweak to the timetable, sometimes a change to a stop, sometimes a deeper rethink. You'll do this in our own tooling: we don't rely on third-party network planning software, and you'll work closely with our engineers to make that tooling better with every route you run through it.

We're serious about AI as a tool. You'll have access to frontier models from Anthropic, OpenAI and others with generous usage limits, and we expect you to use them to move faster on data work and analysis. Being AI-native isn't a substitute for being good — you're accountable for the routes you design and the timetables you launch.

What you might work on

You’ll work on a mixture of greenfield and brownfield projects. That could include:

  • Designing and launching new intercity routes in new geographies — picking the corridor, understanding the existing alternatives, working out charging patterns, building the timetable and getting it registered with the Traffic Commissioner.

  • Re-engineering the timetable on one of our busier routes so we can provide higher passenger utility without adding vehicles, using booking, occupancy and traffic data to find the slack.

  • Building tools that let us run more of the network with less effort — whether that's simulating a proposed timetable against historical demand before we commit to it, or automating the parts of route launch that currently eat days of analyst time.


Diversity and equality

At Ember, we support diversity across our team and customers. We work to ensure every employee feels respected and able to give their best, whether temporary, part-time or full-time. We’re happy to offer flexible working patterns where they make sense, are compassionate when it comes to time off and we offer enhanced maternity and paternity leave.

Read more about our approach in our Equal Opportunities Policy.


What’s on offer

You'll receive a salary of £55,000–£75,000 per annum, depending on your experience and skills, plus share options. You'll be expected to work from our lovely office in central Edinburgh most days — we value in-person communication — but there's flexibility around the odd day from home.

How do I apply?

Send your CV and a short note on why this interests you. We like actions over words, so include a link to something you've built that showcases your skills.


Who we're looking for

You should have a desire to get involved in the growth of a quickly scaling business, with a real opportunity to make your mark. How you work and think matters more to us than specific industry experience. The following should sound a lot like you:

  • Statistically literate. You're an expert in spreadsheets, comfortable with the most complex formulas. You know SQL and/or Python. You have a good grasp of statistics and can use it to make sense of messy real-world data.

  • Grounded. You know when a model is telling you something real and when it's overfitting. You know when a statistically robust result is operationally useless — the right answer for a route isn't always the one with the lowest p-value. Good solutions survive contact with reality and then thrive.

  • AI-native. You treat AI tools as another way to apply your skills. You're comfortable using frontier models to work faster and more rigorously, and you experiment with new tools and techniques as they evolve.

  • Detail-oriented and strategic. Our network is complex, with lots of moving parts that depend on each other. You can zoom in to the detail of a single stop or driver shift, then zoom out to see how a change ripples through the wider system.

  • Interested in transport. You don't need to be a bus spotter, but the problems we're solving should genuinely interest you.

  • Hands-on. This isn't a desk job. You'll get out into the network — riding routes, walking stops, meeting council officers — and you're comfortable blending the strategic, the digital and the real world.

  • Self-managing. You can run several projects at once without things slipping, take initiative on what to prioritise, and jump in to help colleagues across the business when they need it.

Ember is a tech company, not a traditional bus operator. We've built a platform that coordinates our entire operation — everything from monitoring vehicles and controlling chargers to selling tickets and calculating ETAs. This allows us to use electric buses more intensively than anyone else in the world, leading to a massive reduction in emissions. It also helps us provide a much better passenger experience, with innovative features like demand-responsive stops.

The role

Charging hubs are Ember's key growth enabler. They give us the ultra-fast charge points we need to run our network, and they act as a base for our fleet — parking, washing, driver lounges and more. We have hubs across Scotland today, with additional sites across the UK under construction or in the pipeline.

You'll join a small team of four, taking end-to-end responsibility for your own sites and helping out on others. We're typically running a handful of projects at any one time.

Step one is finding a site. You’ll need to think about where we need charging capacity to support future routes, scout industrial estates and brownfield plots and reach out to commercial agents, local authorities and landlords. Some great sites are advertised but many are not, so landing one usually means being patient and creative.

Once you've got a site, we move on to lease negotiations, design, the planning application and the power connection. You'll work with network operators to land the grid connection, and with our suppliers to procure, install and commission the charging equipment. Solicitors, architects and engineers are there to help, but the project is yours to drive — you set the direction, you ask the difficult questions and you make the trade-offs.

It’s important to be hands-on. We don't go to tender and leave the rest to an outsourced project manager — we want you on site, asking why a kerb is in the wrong place. The team keeps refining and improving every site, and you'll be part of that work across the network, not just on the sites you've built yourself.

Diversity and equality

At Ember, we support diversity across our team and customers. We work to ensure every employee feels respected and able to give their best, whether temporary, part-time or full-time. We’re happy to offer flexible working patterns where they make sense, are compassionate when it comes to time off and offer enhanced maternity and paternity leave.

Read more about our approach in our Equal Opportunities Policy.

You'll receive a salary of £55,000–£75,000 per annum, depending on your experience and skills, plus share options. You'll be expected to work from our lovely office in central Edinburgh most days — we value in-person communication — but there's flexibility around the odd day from home, with an expectation that you'll spend some time travelling to different sites.

How do I apply?

Send your CV and a short note on why this interests you.

Applications close Friday 2 October at 5pm.


Who we're looking for

You should have a desire to get involved in the growth of a quickly scaling business, with a real opportunity to make your mark. How you work and think matters more to us than specific industry experience. The following should sound a lot like you:

  • Curious and quick to learn. You're comfortable in unfamiliar territory — new technical specs, new legal terms, new planning processes — and you treat each one as an opportunity to learn. You don't expect to know everything on day one.

  • Engineering mindset. You're the sort of person who'll happily watch YouTube videos explaining concrete reinforcement, three-phase distribution or substation transformers. You'll be excited to dive into the same level of detail on our projects.

  • A first-principles thinker. You take problems back to fundamentals rather than reaching for jargon or the way things are usually done. When you work with experts — solicitors, architects, engineers — you treat them as people you can learn from, not people you can outsource your thinking to.

  • Commercially astute. You can tell when something is worth fighting for and when it's better to redesign around a constraint, whether that's a lease, a planning condition or a contractor's quote.

  • Highly organised. Managing a pipeline of projects is complex, with many timelines, people to chase, details to look into and things that can (and will) go wrong. We want you at Inbox Zero, not in inbox hell.

  • Comfortable using AI. At a minimum you use it as part of how you work — to learn faster, draft documents and get to the bottom of unfamiliar topics. But maybe you’ll go further and build software to help the team work faster and more precisely.

  • Hands-on. Hubs are built in the real world, not behind a screen. You'll meet landlords, talk to electricians and look at drains, but you'll also need to read contracts and chase agents who've gone quiet.

  • A strong sense of what good looks like. Whatever the topic, problem or issue. You need to know how to hold yourself and others to a high standard.

jobs.title: Coach Builder & Smart Repair Technician
jobs.description:
Ember is the UK's first all-electric coach company. We launched in October 2020 and are now running on more than twenty routes – including Dundee to Glasgow, Aberdeen to Edinburgh and Inverness to Fort William – with several further routes launching later in 2026. We are at advanced stages in developing new charging hubs in Kirkcaldy and Glasgow, with many more sites in the pipeline.

As we accelerate our network footprint across Scotland, we are launching a new maintenance and engineering facility in Dundee.

We’re looking for a skilled, reliable and motivated Coach Builder and SMART Repair Technician to join our electric bus maintenance team. This is a hands-on, varied role suited to someone with a practical background who is comfortable working in a busy workshop environment. You won't be expected to be a fully qualified mechanic, but you'll work closely alongside our team of technicians and play a vital part in keeping our zero-emission fleet on the road.

The ideal candidate will be experienced, energetic and confident with the passion to stay on top of the latest developments in the electric vehicle market. This will be a Dundee-based role - but you’ll also be working closely with the teams in Aberdeen, Livingston and Inverness. We’ll make sure that you’re set up for success, with all necessary training, access to the right vehicle and all of the relevant tools and equipment.

This position sits in the middle of bus cosmetic preservation and heavy vehicle structural layout. You will take the lead on end-to-end ownership of bodywork projects—diagnosing alignments, completing structural adjustments, and carrying out surface prep for the panel wrapping team. We need someone who can assess a vehicle and quickly understand exactly how panels and components need to be adjusted or pulled to sit correctly.

This is a truly unique challenge - our coaches are used more intensively than any other electric vehicles in the world so not every problem will have a solution that can be found in a manual. Instead, your team will need to work closely with the manufacturer, go deep into understanding root causes and think creatively about how we could be avoiding the problem altogether in the future.

We’re looking for a problem-solver who will help to identify and resolve issues quickly, and will relish the challenge of joining a new team that will make our state of the art fleet the best-maintained in the country with the lowest downtime.

If you're practical by nature, take pride in your work, and want to build a career in the growing world of electric vehicle maintenance, this could be the perfect opportunity.


Responsibilities

• End-End Ownership: Scope out, manage, and execute repair jobs from initial diagnosis through to final panel alignment and

wrap-ready delivery.

• Panel & Frame Realignment: Look at commercial body frameworks and instinctively figure out structural variances—knowing

what needs to be pulled, moved, or mechanically adjusted this way or that to achieve true lines.

• Wrap Preparation: Execute light bodywork prep, ensuring panels are correctly filled, blocked, sanded, and degreased to

receive high-quality vinyl wrapping.

• SMART Repairs: Resolve local paint defects, deep scratches, scuffs, and minor panel punctures.

• Resource & Parts Estimation: Evaluate damage early to determine the parts required for completion, minimising downtime.

Estimate job timeframes realistically from start to finish.

• HSE Compliance: Maintain a proactive understanding of Health, Safety, and Environment regulations, safely navigating a

workshop environment dedicated to high-voltage electric coaches.

We currently have a team of fifteen employees dedicated to fleet maintenance. You’ll form part of a department that brings all aspects of our maintenance in-house as we continue to grow.

We use technology heavily in the business, primarily building our own software systems. You'll need to be tech-savvy, open to learning new systems and comfortable using remote diagnostics.



You will need to meet these requirements:

  • Technical Background: Experienced Coach Builder or SMART Repair Specialist, ideally bringing a background working with HGVs, PSVs, or heavy commercial coaches, however alternative experience would also be considered.

  • Structural Instinct: A good eye for vehicle geometry; someone who visualises panel alignments and can correct framework

    distortions independently.

  • Operational Autonomy: A self-starter capable of working under their own initiative without needing step-by-step guidance,

    also with strong time management skills to hit fleet deadlines

  • Health & Safety Literacy: A solid understanding for workplace safety standards, handling of equipment, and awareness of

    active workshop environments.

  • Licence: Must hold a valid UK driving licence.

Join a fast-growing company with a purpose! At Fastned, you will actively contribute to accelerating the transition to electric mobility. Together with over 450 colleagues (more than 50  nationalities) across 10 countries, we have big plans: we are building a Europe-wide network of 1,000 beautiful fast-charging stations where electric drivers can charge their cars with energy from the sun and wind. We have recently been voted best charging network in the UK, France, and the Netherlands, a testimony to our drive to offer the best charging experience to EV drivers!

Your role

As a senior member of the UK expansion team, you will drive the growth of Fastned and contribute to our mission: 'Giving freedom to the electric driver".You will work directly alongside the UK Expansion Lead to shape and drive our site acquisition strategy, identifying and securing prime locations, forging strategic partnerships, and continuously raising the bar for how Fastned grows its UK  footprint as we strive towards a European network of 1,000 fast charging stations on prime locations.

  • Contribute to the UK network development strategy: defining target geographies, site typologies, partnership models, and deal structures that maximise long-term network value.

  • Lead the identification, structuring, negotiation, and execution of new EV charging site opportunities across a wide range of counterparties, including commercial landlords, roadside operators, developers, and local authorities, ensuring every transaction is aligned with the network development strategy, commercially robust, and delivered on terms that meet Fastned's financial performance targets.

  • Lead complex, high-value negotiations independently and with commercial authority, structuring leasehold, freehold, and licence agreements that deliver on both strategic and financial targets, while spearheading our drive towards securing flagship locations across the country. 

  • Own and actively manage a portfolio of contracted and pipeline sites, maintaining rigorous discipline over deal timelines, commercial terms, and internal reporting standards. 

  • Work cross-functionally with design, planning, construction, legal, and operations teams to ensure seamless transition from signed agreement through to live station.

  • Drive continuous improvement of the team's processes, tools, data and market intelligence to prioritise effort on the highest-value opportunities.

  • Have a keen eye for market developments and knowledge of when to take advantage of the right opportunities. This includes monitoring policy development and understanding its impact on our development plans. 

  • Help the team structure and streamline processes as much as possible to maximise effectiveness & efficiency.

  • In this role you need to feel comfortable diving into techno-economic topics (together with our subject experts), as you need to know your part when leading negotiations. Your onboarding will include a variety of “masterclasses” around the topics of e-mobility and fast-charging. 

  • Embrace an ambassadorial approach to representing Fastned externally at industry events and trade shows, as well as during day-to-day negotiations.

  • Bring creative, outside-the-box thinking to how we structure partnerships and unlock sites that others cannot. 

We are open to finding our next Expansion Manager in one of the cities mentioned in the vacancy (London, Manchester, Liverpool, Birmingham, Glasgow, Edinburgh, or Newcastle), with regular visits to our London office to work closely with the rest of the team!

Is electromobility new territory for you? No problem! As part of your onboarding, you will take part in a series of exciting workshops where you will learn everything you need to know about electromobility and fast-charging infrastructure.

Who are we looking for

You are a high-impact dealmaker with deep roots in the UK commercial property market and the strategic instincts of a leader. You bring a level of professional maturity that allows you to operate with autonomy, challenge the status quo, and bring others with you. You bring along extensive experience with negotiations in commercial real estate, ideally in site acquisition with private landowners, agents, and governmental bodies.

You are keen to communicate Fastned's vision and values to site owners & real estate companies and support your team in its expansion. Additionally, you tick the following boxes:

  • 5+  years of relevant experience in commercial real estate site acquisition or development, ideally within roadside, retail, infrastructure, energy, or a similarly complex real estate environment.

  • Chartered Surveyor (MRICS), or demonstrable equivalent professional standing.

  • Strong negotiation and problem-solving skills.

  • An established and active network of relevant stakeholders across UK property, including landowners, commercial developers, and local authorities. 

  • Comfortable managing dozens of projects simultaneously, at different stages of development, each with their own deadlines and individual stakeholders. 

  • Outstanding stakeholder management skills.

  • Outstanding written and verbal communication skills: able to present with conviction to both internal leadership and external C-suite counterparts.

  • Open for regular travel within the United Kingdom and occasional travel to continental Europe.

  • You’re an outgoing person who enjoys seeing new places and meeting new people.

Nice-to-have…

  • Directly relevant experience in ultra-rapid EV charging is not a pre-requisite, but it is a positive. 

  • Experience with grid connections and work with DNOs, IDNOs and ICPs. 

  • Experience with the UK planning system (NPPF, permitted development rights) as it relates to EV infrastructure or energy assets.

  • Plus points for previous experience in fast growth companies or renewable energy.

  • Strong financial literacy: you know your way around a financial model, understand yield, IRR, and NPV in the context of a site acquisition, and hold your own in conversations with investment-minded counterparties.

  • Highly motivated to accelerate the energy transition: you genuinely care about contributing to the UK’s drive towards electric car adoption, renewable energy and the improvement of air quality. 

Join us in building a better future

We are on a mission to make a positive impact, but we don't forget to recognise & celebrate our successes, big and small. We put a focus on work-life balance, provide you with genuine work flexibility and have family-friendly policies in place. Our core benefits include:

  • Stock option plan -> we believe in shared value creation.

  • A training and development budget of £2,600 per year per employee, because development and training are important to us, and our sector offers endless opportunities.

  • 29 holidays. Additionally, we give you two mission days you can use to contribute to Fastned’s mission or to support a cause that is important to you.

  • In order to find some new sites & enjoy the EV life, we will provide you with your own EV car with charging expenses covered.

  • A paid pension plan, fully covered by Fastned.

  • Full health and dental cover via  Bupa.

  • Daily commuting costs to the office are reimbursed.

  • Daily vegetarian lunches, snacks, and drinks are provided at our office.

  • Weekly CrossFit classes with a trained professional.

  • Mental Wellbeing with nilo health: Access to a confidential mental health platform offering 1-on-1 coaching with psychologists, group sessions, and a variety of digital self-care tools

  • Physical Wellbeing with Wellhub: Enjoy a sponsored membership providing flexible access to a vast network of local gyms, fitness classes, and premium digital apps for wellness and nutrition.

  • Going the extra mile for parents: We provide you with personalised coaching support before, during, and after parental leave, facilitated by Foundree.

  • In addition to fun events year-round, we throw notorious Christmas parties, annual ski trips and organise an amazing yearly trip abroad with all employees.

Interested? Apply today!

We would love to have a conversation with you! Apply now, send us your CV and explain in your motivation letter why you’re excited about joining our mission to provide freedom to electric drivers and speeding up the energy transition.

The recruitment process consists of these stages below:

  • A first video call with our recruiter to find out more about Fastned & our company culture;

  • A second case-interview with the Expansion Lead UK and another member of the pipeline team;

  • An office visit to meet members of the Expansion and wider London team!

Then, it’s time to welcome you on board to Fastned!

Fastned stands for equity and inclusion. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, gender identities, sexual orientations, religions, neurodiversity, disabilities, parental status or any other protected characteristic that makes you unique.

jobs.title: Senior DevOps Engineer
jobs.description:
The Senior DevOps Engineer is responsible for the development, maintenance, and optimisation of Bromcom’s Microsoft Azure infrastructure. Reporting to the DevOps Team Lead, this role plays a key part in ensuring the stability, security, and scalability of the organisation’s cloud platform.

This is a hands-on technical role with responsibility for delivering infrastructure, improving automation, maintaining CI/CD pipelines, and supporting platform reliability. The role requires a proactive approach to problem-solving and continuous improvement across Azure and DevOps practices.

Key Responsibilities

Azure Infrastructure

  • Design, deploy, and maintain Microsoft Azure resources and services 

  • Implement and manage Infrastructure as Code (Terraform, Bicep, ARM or similar) 

  • Ensure Azure environments are secure, scalable, and highly available 

  • Perform platform maintenance, upgrades, and continuous improvements 

CI/CD & Automation

  • Build, maintain, and improve CI/CD pipelines (Azure DevOps preferred) 

  • Automate deployment and operational processes to reduce manual effort 

  • Troubleshoot and resolve pipeline and deployment issues 

  • Drive improvements in release reliability and deployment efficiency 

Monitoring & Incident Management

  • Monitor platform health, performance, and availability 

  • Investigate and resolve production incidents in a timely manner 

  • Perform root cause analysis and implement preventative measures 

  • Enhance logging, alerting, and observability across the platform 

Security & Governance

  • Implement Azure security best practices and policies 

  • Manage identity and access controls in line with governance standards 

  • Ensure compliance with engineering standards and change management processes 

  • Contribute to cost optimisation and efficient resource usage 

Collaboration & Continuous Improvement

  • Work closely with developers, DevOps engineers, and technical leads 

  • Participate in planning, stand-ups, and technical discussions 

  • Maintain and improve infrastructure and process documentation 

  • Contribute to continuous improvement of DevOps practices and tooling 

Skills & Experience

Essential

  • Proven experience working in a DevOps, Cloud, or Platform Engineering role for 5+ years

  • Hands-on experience with Microsoft Azure (App Services, networking, storage, identity, etc.) 

  • Experience with Infrastructure as Code (Terraform, Bicep, ARM or similar) 

  • Strong experience with CI/CD pipelines (Azure DevOps, GitHub Actions, or similar) 

  • Good understanding of cloud networking concepts (DNS, routing, load balancing, firewalls) 

  • Experience with monitoring and logging tools (Application Insights, Log Analytics, etc.) 

  • Ability to troubleshoot production issues across infrastructure and application layers 

  • Understanding of security best practices (identity management, least privilege, secure configs) 

  • Familiarity with source control (Git) and modern development workflows 

Desirable

  • Knowledge of scripting languages (PowerShell, Bash, or Python) 

  • Experience working with Azure Front Door, WAF, or CDN technologies 

  • Exposure to observability tooling (distributed tracing, metrics platforms) 

  • Experience with cost management and optimisation in Azure 

  • Understanding of DevOps principles and Agile delivery practices 

Personal Attributes

  • Strong problem-solving skills with a proactive mindset 

  • Ability to work independently and manage priorities effectively 

  • Good communication and collaboration skills 

  • Keen interest in learning and developing cloud and DevOps expertise

jobs.title: DevOps Team Manager
jobs.description:
Bromcom Computers Plc is the UK's fastest-growing cloud-native school Management Information System (MIS) provider, serving thousands of schools across three UK countries. The DevOps Team Manager leads a team of 3-4 engineers and is accountable for the reliable, secure and controlled operation of Bromcom's Azure-first SaaS platform. This is a hands-on DevOps engineering leadership role with an expected balance of 70% hands-on DevOps engineering and 30% people and team management. The manager works closely with the engineers, contributes directly to delivery and operations, and owns completion and ongoing maintenance of the agreed DevOps operational control improvements.

The role requires a credible engineering background. The successful candidate is expected to work directly across Azure platform engineering, CI/CD, Bicep/ARM, automation, incident response and operational controls, while leading the team and setting standards. They must be able to challenge technical decisions, understand operational risk and failure modes, and ensure agreed processes are implemented, followed, evidenced and continually improved. A control is not complete simply because a policy or tool exists; it must work consistently in practice.

Key Responsibilities

People & Team Leadership

  • Lead, line-manage and develop a team of 3-4 DevOps engineers, including at least one senior engineer; own recruitment, onboarding, objectives, appraisals and performance management.

  • Set clear role boundaries, decision rights and escalation routes; ensure high-risk activities are performed or approved only by people with the required competence and authority.

  • Own team capacity, priorities and the out-of-hours on-call rota. The manager is expected to take a fair share of scheduled rota cover alongside the engineers and respond to production incidents and urgent operational issues during that cover, including evenings, weekends and bank holidays where required. Ensure rota coverage, handovers, escalation routes and recovery time are planned and sustainable, while protecting time for reliability, control improvement, technical debt, training and documentation.

  • Build an accountable coaching culture in which engineers raise risk early, follow agreed standards, maintain evidence and learn from incidents and control failures.

Engineering & Platform Leadership

  • Provide hands-on engineering leadership for Bromcom's Azure-hosted, multi-tenant SaaS platform. Work closely with engineers to design, build, review, troubleshoot and improve platform services, pipelines, Infrastructure-as-Code, automation and operational tooling. The manager remains accountable for technical quality while enabling engineers to own their work.

  • Set and maintain engineering standards for Azure architecture, Azure DevOps, Bicep/ARM, deployment patterns, observability, resilience, security and operational support.

  • Challenge designs and changes using risk, maintainability, failure-mode, rollback and supportability thinking; involve senior engineers and technical leadership where specialist authority is required.

  • Own platform SLAs/SLOs, service health, major-incident command, root-cause analysis, disaster recovery, business continuity testing and continuous service improvement.

Operational Controls, Standards & Compliance

  • Take day-to-day ownership within the DevOps team for implementing the agreed operational control improvement plan, driving actions to completion and then maintaining the controls as part of normal team operation.

  • Implement and enforce an end-to-end change lifecycle covering request, design, risk assessment, peer or senior review, testing, approval, implementation, post-change verification and formal closure.

  • Ensure policies, standard operating procedures, runbooks, RACI and ownership arrangements, approval thresholds and evidence requirements remain current, practical and aligned across Azure DevOps, SysAid and other operational systems.

  • Ensure production and customer-impacting changes, including emergency changes and customer-specific change notices, have proportionate risk classification, segregation of duties, pre-production evidence, approval, rollback plans and traceable outcomes.

  • Maintain audit-ready evidence for changes, deployments, access, incidents, disaster-recovery tests, vulnerabilities, exceptions and corrective actions, aligned with Bromcom's security, quality, service-management, UK GDPR and customer obligations.

  • Confirm controls are operating effectively, not simply documented or configured. Track exceptions, overdue actions and repeat failures to closure, with clear corrective actions and independent assurance where required.

  • Provide weekly control reporting and escalate material risk, blocked actions or insufficient capacity promptly. Work with QA, Compliance, Security and technical leads to translate procedural controls into automated technical gates where practical.

Delivery, Automation & AI

  • Work directly with engineers to design, build, review and continually improve Azure DevOps CI/CD pipelines and Bicep/ARM Infrastructure-as-Code, including automated approvals, testing, security checks, evidence capture and post-deployment verification.

  • Reduce manual toil and unsafe variation through automation, reusable platform patterns and clear service ownership; ensure manual exceptions are visible, justified, time-bound and reviewed.

  • Set the strategy and guardrails for AI-assisted and agentic DevOps delivery across CI/CD, Infrastructure-as-Code generation, incident triage, log analysis, runbook automation and documentation.

  • Use and govern AI engineering tools such as Claude, GitHub Copilot or Codex, with clear quality, security, data-protection and human accountability controls. Apply them practically to increase delivery speed, quality and reliability, while ensuring an engineer remains accountable for every output and change.

Security, Identity & FinOps

  • Own platform identity, privileged-access and secrets-management controls, including Entra ID, Key Vault, OAuth, certificate automation, WAF and network security across VNets, App Gateway, S2S VPN and DNS.

  • Ensure access follows least-privilege principles, is reviewed regularly and is supported by effective joiner-mover-leaver, break-glass and segregation-of-duties controls.

  • Own observability standards across Azure Monitor and Grafana, security and vulnerability follow-up, and cloud cost and FinOps accountability for the Azure estate.

Stakeholder & Cross-Team Influence

  • Act as the accountable management and technical escalation point across Software Engineering, CloudOps, IT and Security, QA and Compliance, and external partners, working with senior engineers on design-authority decisions.

  • Provide concise, conclusions-first reporting to the CTO and Executive Team on service health, delivery, control effectiveness, risks, exceptions and improvement progress.

  • Contribute to Bromcom's software delivery transformation programme and align the DevOps operating model and controls with AIDP and wider software-engineering standards.

Person Specification

Essential

  • Proven line-management experience leading a DevOps, CloudOps or platform team, with accountability for recruitment, objectives, appraisals, development and performance management.

  • Current hands-on experience in DevOps, cloud or platform engineering, with the ability to contribute directly to architecture, Azure platform work, pipelines, Bicep/ARM Infrastructure-as-Code, automation, troubleshooting, security and resilience. Candidates should expect approximately 70% of the role to involve hands-on engineering delivery.

  • Evidence of implementing and maintaining operational controls, processes and procedures in a DevOps or CloudOps environment, including ownership of improvement actions, exceptions, corrective actions and audit evidence.

  • Practical command of end-to-end change and release governance, including risk classification, peer or senior review, testing, approvals, segregation of duties, rollback, emergency change, post-change verification and closure.

  • Deep Azure platform expertise across Entra ID, App Services, Key Vault, App Gateway, VNets, Azure SQL or MySQL, WAF and DNS.

  • Strong CI/CD and Infrastructure-as-Code knowledge across Azure DevOps pipelines and Bicep/ARM for Windows and Linux workloads, with the ability to govern standards and technical gates.

  • A track record of operating production, multi-tenant SaaS at scale, including SLA/SLO ownership, major-incident command, root-cause analysis, disaster recovery and service improvement. Willingness and ability to participate personally in the out-of-hours on-call rota, including scheduled evening, weekend and bank-holiday cover where required.

  • Experience working with security, compliance and audit teams in a regulated or data-sensitive environment, with the ability to turn policies into workable controls and demonstrate that they operate effectively.

  • Demonstrable practical use of Claude, GitHub Copilot or Codex as engineering delivery tools, with sound governance, secure use and accountable human review.

  • Clear senior-level communication and reporting, with the discipline to assign owners, manage risks and dependencies, challenge weak evidence and pursue actions through to verified closure.

Desirable

  • Experience leading an operational-control improvement or remediation programme in an ISO 27001 or similarly controlled environment.

  • Containerisation and orchestration experience across AKS or Kubernetes and Docker for multi-tenant workloads.

  • Knowledge of ITIL or service-management controls and practical use of service desk or work-management platforms such as SysAid.

  • Experience in education, public sector, health, finance or another data-sensitive sector, including familiarity with UK GDPR and customer-specific change controls.

  • Relevant certification, such as Azure Solutions Architect Expert or DevOps Engineer Expert.

jobs.title: .NET Full-Stack Developer
jobs.description:

Our mission is to transform the way educational organisations work by providing secure, intuitive and innovative technology that helps schools operate more efficiently and enables educators to focus on what matters most – delivering outstanding outcomes for children and young people.

As Bromcom continues to grow, we are investing in our people, products and technology to support our ambitious plans for the future. This is an exciting opportunity to join a growing technology team and play a key role in developing and enhancing solutions used by education organisations across the UK.

The Role

The .NET Full-Stack Developer is responsible for developing, maintaining and enhancing web applications across both backend and frontend technologies.

Working as part of a collaborative development team, the role will contribute to the design and delivery of reliable, scalable and maintainable software solutions. The successful candidate will have a solid foundation in full-stack development, with particular experience in .NET and C#, alongside the ability and enthusiasm to learn and work with new technologies as required.

The role will also involve using AI-assisted development tools to support software development, including code generation, troubleshooting, testing and productivity. The successful candidate will be comfortable working alongside AI tools while applying their own technical knowledge and judgement to review, validate and refine AI-generated outputs.

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop reliable and scalable backend services and APIs using .NET and C#.

  • Contribute to frontend development using modern web technologies and frameworks.

  • Use AI-assisted development tools to support coding, debugging, testing, research and problem-solving.

  • Participate in code reviews, testing and debugging activities to maintain high standards of software quality.

  • Work collaboratively with Business Analysts, Developers, QA and other stakeholders throughout the software development lifecycle.

  • Contribute to continuous improvement of development processes, practices and technical solutions.

  • Quickly learn and apply new technologies, tools, frameworks and AI-assisted development approaches where required.

  • Support the delivery of high-quality software within agreed timescales.

Skills & Experience

Essential

  • Practical experience in full-stack software development.

  • Strong working knowledge of .NET and C#.

  • Experience developing web applications and backend services/APIs.

  • Understanding of frontend development and modern web technologies.

  • Good understanding of software development principles and practices.

  • Experience or demonstrated ability to work effectively with AI-assisted development tools, using them to support coding, debugging, testing and problem-solving.

  • Ability to critically review and validate AI-generated code and suggestions, ensuring outputs are secure, accurate, maintainable and aligned with development standards.

  • Strong underlying software development fundamentals, with the ability to understand, adapt and take ownership of AI-assisted outputs.

  • Experience working collaboratively within a software development team.

Desirable

Personal Attributes

  • Collaborative – comfortable working with developers, QA, Business Analysts and wider stakeholders.

  • Quality focused – takes pride in producing reliable, maintainable and well-tested code.

  • Proactive – willing to contribute ideas and look for opportunities to improve processes and solutions.

  • A strong communicator – able to explain technical issues and work effectively with both technical and non-technical colleagues.

jobs.title: Technical Quality Assurance Manager
jobs.description:
The Technical QA Manager is responsible for the technical direction, governance and continual improvement of quality engineering across the organisation’s delivery areas.

The role defines and maintains the overarching test strategy and ensures that quality engineering practices are practical, risk-based and integrated throughout the software delivery lifecycle.

The Technical QA Manager provides direct technical leadership and support to QA Champions and Test Automation Engineers. The role ensures that team testing strategies, automation approaches, quality standards and release evidence are aligned, measurable and consistently applied.

The purpose of the Technical QA Manager role is to:

· Define, communicate and maintain the organisational test strategy and supporting quality engineering standards.

· Enable QA Champions to define and operate effective team and product-area testing strategies.

· Provide technical direction to Test Automation Engineers on automation strategy, framework design, coding standards, CI/CD integration, reusable components, maintainability, diagnostics, test data and execution reliability.

· Ensure automated test execution is embedded into delivery pipelines and provides fast, reliable and actionable feedback.

· Align functional, integration, regression, non-functional and release validation with product, technical and delivery risk.

· Strengthen developer ownership of testing while providing appropriate governance, coaching and assurance.

· Ensure AI-generated testing assets and automation code are reviewed critically before use.

· Defining expectations for pipeline triggers, test execution, quality controls, test-result publication, diagnostic information and failure feedback.

· Ensuring pipeline automation is reliable, maintainable and proportionate to product and release risk.

· Improve release confidence through clear, evidence-based quality and automation reporting.

· Reduce avoidable rework, escaped defects, flaky tests and dependency on manual regression testing.

The Technical QA Manager should be able to:

· Define and implement comprehensive, risk-based test strategies across multiple delivery areas.

· Translate organisational quality objectives into practical engineering standards.

· Demonstrate practical integration of automated tests into CI/CD pipelines.

· Define effective pipeline execution, result visibility and failure-feedback approaches.

· Provide credible technical leadership on modern test automation frameworks.

· Work effectively with Playwright or equivalent test automation technology.

· Review and guide maintainable automation code.

· Understand automation developed using C#, Java or an equivalent object-oriented language.

· Understand functional, integration, regression, API, user-interface and relevant non-functional testing approaches.

· Assess the suitability of automation at different levels of a system.

· Review automation framework design, test architecture and reusable components.

· Evaluate automation maintainability, test data, environment dependencies and execution reliability.

· Identify flaky, duplicated, low-value or overly expensive automated tests.

· Analyse quality and automation evidence to identify systemic risks and improvement priorities.

· Understand risk management, risk identification and risk-based testing.

· Coach and influence QA Champions, Test Automation Engineers, developers and delivery stakeholders.

· Communicate technical quality risks clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.

· Challenge weak requirements, ineffective controls and poor automation practices constructively.

· Use AI-assisted testing capabilities critically, with appropriate review, traceability and governance.

The successful candidate should have:

·         Strong experience in software quality assurance, test automation and quality engineering.

·         Experience providing technical leadership across complex software delivery environments using kaban methodology.

·         Demonstrable experience integrating automated test suites into CI/CD pipelines.

·         Demonstrable experience improving the reliability and feedback value of pipeline-based automated testing.

·         Proven ability to define, implement and govern testing strategies.

·         Experience supporting other quality roles in applying testing strategies within delivery teams.

·         Practical experience with a modern automation framework.

·         Preferable experience with Playwright and Selenium.

·         Practical coding capability in an object-oriented programming language.

·         Experience designing, building or significantly improving maintainable test automation frameworks.

·         Experience reviewing automation architecture and test-code quality.

·         A good understanding of functional, integration, regression and release testing.

·         A good understanding of software delivery lifecycle and release governance.

·         A good understanding of risk management, risk identification and risk-based testing.

·         A proactive and improvement-focused approach.

·         The confidence to challenge poor quality or automation practices constructively.

Desirable experience includes:

·         Experience with Azure DevOps pipelines.

·         Experience configuring automated test execution within build and deployment pipelines.

·         Experience publishing and interpreting automated test results within CI/CD tooling.

·         Experience implementing pipeline quality controls.

The Technical QA Manager should be measured on:

·         Adoption and effectiveness of organisational testing strategy.

·         Quality and consistency of team and product-area testing strategies.

·         Effectiveness of support provided to QA Champions.

·         Effectiveness of technical direction provided to Test Automation Engineers.

·         Reliable automated test execution within CI/CD pipelines.

·         Faster, clearer and more actionable quality feedback to delivery teams.

·         Increased useful automated coverage in areas of meaningful product risk.

·         Reduced flaky, duplicated and low-value automated tests.

·         Improved maintainability of automation frameworks and test code.

·         Reduced dependency on repeatable manual regression testing.

·         Reduced escaped defects and avoidable rework.

·         Improved developer ownership of testing and quality.

·         Improved compliance with agreed Definition of Done expectations and release control processes.

·         Clear and evidence-based release-readiness reporting.

·         Timely escalation of significant quality and automation risks.

·         Improved collaboration between QA Champions, Test Automation Engineers and developers.

·         Demonstrable improvement in release confidence and testing effectiveness.

·         Success should not be measured only by the volume of tests automated. Measures consider automation value, reliability, risk coverage, feedback speed, maintainability and model.

jobs.title: Sjuksköterska till plastik- och käkkirurgisk avdelning, 85F2
jobs.description:
Verksamhetsområde plastik- och käkkirurgi

Vi är Akademiska sjukhuset – ett av Sveriges ledande universitetssjukhus. Som länssjukhus och leverantör av högspecialiserad vård erbjuder vi vård till två miljoner människor i Mellansverige. Här händer det ständigt något – ett nytt liv föds, en mormor opereras, en kollega hyllas som hjälte. Hos oss får du uppleva både hårda prövningar och fantastiska händelser, i en stark gemenskap med kollegor. Välkommen med din ansökan!

Vår verksamhet
Detta arbete är för dig som gillar att ha stor bredd, omväxling och vill lära dig nya färdigheter. Avdelning 85F2 är en kirurgisk vårdavdelning med inriktning mot plastik- och käkkirurgi samt brännskadevård på en och samma avdelning. Vi vårdar både vuxna och barn med ett intag av patienter som är både planerat och akut. Patienter med behov av särskild högspecialiserad vård tas emot från vårt eget län, den region vi ansvarar för i egenskap av universitetssjukhus, från hela riket samt även från utlandet.  

Vi erbjuder ett varierande arbete med utmaningar och stor stimulans som bidrar till utveckling av din kompetens. I vår specialitet återskapas funktionalitet efter tex. tumörsjukdomar, svåra kroppsskador såsom brännskador och medfödda missbildningar. Den rekonstruktiva plastikkirurgin vid Akademiska sjukhuset är erkänd som ett av de ledande centren inom plastikkirurgi både nationellt och internationellt.

Dina kvalifikationer
Du är legitimerad sjuksköterska med ett intresse av kirurgisk vård. Du är driven, lösningsorienterad och nyfiken som person. Ditt motto är att alltid göra det bästa för patienten. Erfarenheter inom kirurgisk vård och/eller vård av barn är meriterande men inte ett krav.

Vi erbjuder
Vi söker en ny sjuksköterska till vårt team. Vi erbjuder en tillsvidareanställning på två eller treskift. Vid treskift så erhålls rotationstillägg.

Du kommer att få en inskolning på ca 6 veckor tillsammans med en handledare, introduktionen anpassas till dina förkunskaper så att du ska känna dig trygg i din roll hos oss.  Vi överenskommer med dig hur arbetstiderna under inskolning ska se ut. Vi tycker att det är viktigt med en individuell inskolning då vi alla har olika behov. Kontinuerlig kompetensutveckling under karriären är en självklarhet för oss.

Hos oss får du förmåner som gör skillnad, läs om förmånerna här (https://regionuppsala.se/formaner/).

Vill du veta mer?
Avdelningschef Sabina Lindberg, sabina.lindberg@akademiska.se, 018-611 54 26
Fackförbund nås via Region Uppsalas växel 018-611 00 00.

Vill du jobba med oss?
Välkommen med din ansökan via länken nedan. Intervjuer sker fortlöpande under ansökningstiden så tjänsten kan därför tillsättas innan sista ansökningsdatum. Sök redan idag

Läs om anställningsvillkor och lönesättning inom Region Uppsala här: Bli vår nya kollega (https://regionuppsala.se/jobb-och-utbildning/bli-var-nya-kollega/)

Region Uppsala värdesätter de kvaliteter som jämn könsfördelning och mångfald tillför verksamheten och ser gärna sökande av alla kön och med olika födelsebakgrund, funktionalitet och livserfarenhet.

Region Uppsala krigsplacerar all tillsvidareanställd personal utifrån totalförsvarets behov. Detta innebär för den enskilda medarbetaren inga förpliktelser i fredstid utan är enkom en planeringsåtgärd.

Inför beslut om anställning, sker kontroll av misstanke- och belastningsregister avseende samtliga arbetssökanden som i den sökta anställningen kan komma att arbeta inom psykiatrisk sjukvård, habilitering, vård av barn och ungdom eller tvångsvård av missbrukare, områden som omfattas av fakultativa registerutdrag. Detta gäller således alla som kommer att arbeta patientnära, även om arbetsuppgifterna i nuläget inte är tänkta att huvudsakligen innehålla arbete med ovan nämnda patientgrupper.

Denna rekrytering sker helt genom Region Uppsalas försorg och vi undanber oss telefonsamtal från rekryteringsföretag och annonsförsäljare.

jobs.title: Engagerad skolbibliotekarie
jobs.description:
Vi söker dig som vill vara med och forma morgondagens Ale. Hos oss är du med och levererar service och tjänster av bästa kvalitet till Aleborna. Tillsammans skapar 2 500 medarbetare ett Ale, kommunen som fokuserar på invånarna och deras behov. Bli en av oss!

Om arbetsplatsen

Vill du vara med och utveckla framtidens skolbibliotek och skapa de bästa förutsättningarna för barns och ungas lärande? Då kan detta vara uppdraget för dig.

Ale kommun har under ett och ett halvt år gjort en resa från att inte ha några skolbibliotekarier till att ha två och en halv tjänst. Vi söker därför dig som vill vara med och utveckla bibliotekets pedagogiska roll och bidra till att skolbiblioteket blir en självklar del av elevernas lärande och skolans utvecklingsarbete.

Arbetsuppgifter

Vi söker en engagerad, kreativ och utvecklingsinriktad skolbibliotekarie till ett tidsbegränsat vikariat på våra skolor i norra Ale. Hos oss får du ett meningsfullt uppdrag där du bidrar till att stärka elevernas läsning, språkutveckling, informationskompetens och lust att lära. Vi ser skolbiblioteket som en strategisk resurs i skolans verksamhet och som en viktig del av arbetet för ökad måluppfyllelse, likvärdig utbildning och språkutveckling.

Som skolbibliotekarie arbetar du nära skolornas pedagogiska arbete. Du inspirerar till läsning och litteraturupplevelser, stödjer elevernas utveckling av källkritik och informationssökning samt bidrar med kompetens inom medie- och informationskunnighet i en allt mer digital värld. Du ansvarar för bibliotekets mediebestånd och lärmiljö samtidigt som du driver och utvecklar läsfrämjande insatser som väcker nyfikenhet, engagemang och framtidstro hos våra elever.

Kvalifikationer

Vi söker särskilt dig som har kunskap om barns och ungas läsutveckling och som ser sambandet mellan läsning, språk och lärande. Våra medarbetare efterfrågar en kollega som kan bidra med pedagogiska perspektiv och vara ett stöd i arbetet med att utveckla elevernas läsförmåga och läsmotivation. Vi ser därför gärna att du har erfarenhet av att samverka med pedagoger kring läsfrämjande arbete, språk- och kunskapsutvecklande arbetssätt eller andra insatser som stärker elevers lärande.

Du har utbildning inom biblioteks- och informationsvetenskap eller annan utbildning som arbetsgivaren bedömer som likvärdig. Erfarenhet av skolbibliotek eller arbete i skola är meriterande, men vi lägger också stor vikt vid ditt engagemang, din samarbetsförmåga och din vilja att utveckla verksamheten.

För att trivas hos oss behöver du vara initiativrik, självgående och relationsskapande. Du ser möjligheter, vågar tänka nytt och har förmåga att omsätta idéer till praktik. Du har ett inkluderande förhållningssätt och tror på litteraturens och kunskapens kraft att öppna dörrar för alla elever, oavsett bakgrund och förutsättningar.

Hos oss får du möjlighet att göra verklig skillnad varje dag. Du blir en del av en verksamhet där elevens bästa alltid står i centrum och där vi värdesätter samarbete, kvalitet, utveckling och modet att pröva nya vägar.

Övrigt

Välkommen med din ansökan och bli en del av Ale kommuns fortsatta satsning på skolbibliotek som stärker läsning, lärande och framtidstro för alla elever.

Työtehtävät ovat monipuolisia ravintola-alan tehtäviä, ja pääset osallistumaan laajasti ravintolan toimintaan, prosesseihin sekä arjen sujuvuuden varmistamiseen. Tarjoamme sinulle ainutlaatuisen mahdollisuuden olla mukana rakentamassa ja avaamassa aivan uutta ravintolakokonaisuutta. Hyviä vuorovaikutustaitoja ja kykyä innostaa muita

Mahdollisuuden olla mukana avaamassa uutta ravintolamaailmaa ja kehittämässä sen toimintaa alusta alkaen
Mahdollisuuden vastaanottaa lisätyötä, osaaminen huomioiden

Saat arvokasta kokemusta esihenkilötyöstä, ravintolamaailman avaamisesta sekä mahdollisuuden kehittää omaa osaamistasi kohti tulevia vaativampia vastuutehtäviä.

jobs.title: Migrationshandläggare till mottagning- och återvändandecenter i Malmö
jobs.description:
Vi söker flera migrationshandläggare inom mottagning, boende och återvändandecenter som ligger i Malmö och Burlöv. Inrättandet av center är en del av den nationella reformeringen av asylmottagandet i samband med asylpaktens genomförande. Detta är en roll för dig som är nyfiken på en ny utmaning och som trivs med varierade arbetsuppgifter, ingå i ett team och arbeta på schema.

Beskrivning av center

Center är en ny typ av arbetsplats. Du arbetar med frågor som berör och engagerar i en dynamisk miljö som präglas av mötet med människor och som påverkas av vad som händer i vår omvärld. Det är också en miljö som präglas av kontinuerligt lärande och delaktighet och där vi genom samlokalisering har bättre förutsättningar för att arbeta nära varandra mellan professionerna i asylprocessen. Vi är även nära den asylsökande genom att vi arbetar där den asylsökande bor. Därigenom kan vi arbeta effektivare och göra det tryggare för den asylsökande.

Det är en internationell miljö, både genom att det är nära Kastrups flygplats där de flesta anländer till och lämnar Sverige, men även genom att myndigheten under nästa år blir mer integrerade i ett gemensamt europeiskt asylmottagande och EU-myndigheter som Frontex och EUAA. När du arbetar i center blir du en del av resan mot ett nytt och reformerat asylmottagande. Du förväntas vara öppen för att din kompetens och ditt engagemang behövs inom olika arbetsuppgifter som utförs på centret, där inte minst service och vägledning är att genomgående inslag. Gå gärna in och lyssna på vår podd, där bland annat två erfarna teamledare på Migrationsverkets boende, delar med sig av hur det är att arbeta nära människor som söker skydd i Sverige; här



Vad gör en migrationshandläggare?I din roll som migrationshandläggare på center har du mycket kontakt med personer som bor där. Du kommer också i kontakt med andra intressenter som vistas på center och även andra myndigheter. Som migrationshandläggare arbetar du med att handlägga, utreda, besluta och ta fram förslag till beslut i olika typer av ärenden. Besluten har rättslig verkan för enskilda personer och påverkar deras rätt till förmåner, rättigheter och skyldigheter. Därutöver arbetar du med administration där du hanterar akter och handlingar som har kommit in eller upprättats i ett ärende. I din roll möter du och har samtal med personer som har ett ärende hos Migrationsverket och andra intressenter. Samtalen kan handla om att underrätta om beslut eller informera om Migrationsverkets processer samt vägleda och ge service. Du identifierar och hanterar eventuella särskilda behov hos personer och i förekommande fall håller du samtal med vuxna och barn i utsatta situationer. Verksamheten på center präglas av hög variation av olika arbetsuppgifter och förmågan att arbeta tillsammans med andra i grupp är viktig. Verksamheten pågår dygnet runt.



Vem är du?Vi söker dig som har en god samarbetsförmåga, är lyhörd och kommunicerar på ett konstruktivt sätt. Du är tydlig i din kommunikation och säkerställer att budskap når fram och att förväntningarna är klara för alla berörda parter. Vidare är du strukturerad och självständigt kan planera och organisera arbetet på ett effektivt sätt mot uppsatta mål och deadline. Du är flexibel och har lätt för att anpassa dig och ändra ditt synsätt och förhållningssätt vid ändrade omständigheter.

I vårt arbete som statstjänstemän ställs även höga krav på omdöme och en hög säkerhets- och sekretessmedvetenhet.



Du som söker har

    Akademisk utbildning om minst 120hp med juridisk, samhällsvetenskaplig eller beteendevetenskaplig inriktning eller annan utbildning i kombination med för rollen aktuell och relevant erfarenhet.
    Kunskap inom förvaltningsrättsliga ärenden.
    Erfarenhet av arbete med krav på god service och professionellt bemötande.
    God kommunikativ förmåga och uttrycker dig väl i tal och skrift på svenska och engelska.
    Goda kunskaper i Officepaketet.



Det är meriterande om du har

    Handläggningsvana.
    Aktuell erfarenhet av arbete med förvaltningsrättsliga ärenden.
    Erfarenhet av att arbeta med människor som befinner sig i en utsatt situation.



Upplysningar

Anställningsform: tillsvidare anställning med provanställning

Arbetstider: Schemalagd arbetstid: 3 skift och 5 veckors schema dag, kväll, natt och helg, för närvarande dag kl. 07-16.30, kväll kl. 11.30-21.00 och helg kl. 09-18.00. Arbetstiderna kan komma att förändras och även innebära arbete nattetid.  

Placering: Malmö

Tillträde: snarast enligt överenskommelse

Anställningsförmåner: Läs om våra anställningsförmåner här.

Tjänsten innebär direkt och regelbunden kontakt med barn. Enligt lag (2013:852) om registerkontroll för personer som ska arbeta med barn ska den som erbjuds anställning, visa upp ett giltigt utdrag ur belastningsregistret.

Urval kan komma att ske löpande men samtliga ansökningar kommer att tas i beaktning efter annonseringsperioden har löpt ut. Om du är aktuell vidare i rekryteringen kommer en digital informationsträff att hållas den 4 eller 5 november. Vi planerar för gruppintervjuer under vecka 46.



Ansökan
