starting on 1 January 2027, or as otherwise agreed, by 1 September 2027 at the latest. The position is based in Helsinki within the subject of Statistics, which is part of the Department of Finance and Economics.

The position is part of Hankens tenure-track system and is open to researchers with the potential for an outstanding academic career. If the position is filled at the Assistant Professor or Associate Professor level, the successful candidate will have the opportunity to advance through evaluations that consider merits across all relevant areas in accordance with [Hankens tenure track guidelines](https://www.hanken.fi/en/faculty-staff/job-opportunities/job-opportunities/hankens-tenure-track-system).

Hanken School of Economics is a research-oriented business school offering education in Swedish and English. The Statistics unit, which collaborates closely with Finance and Information Systems, conducts high-quality research on financial time series. The subject seeks to strengthen its teaching and research in the application of machine learning and business analytics. The subject offers education at the Bachelors, Masters, and doctoral levels.

The Department provides a strong research environment, reflected in the growing scope and breadth of its research activities. We value high-quality research with relevance to business and economics, as demonstrated by publications in highly ranked academic journals.

Requirements

The applicants will be reviewed based on their research, teaching, institutional service, and societal impact. Applicants for the current position are required to have a fluent command of both English and Swedish. Teaching in Swedish is expected as part of the position's responsibilities.

Applicants on the assistant professor level should hold a doctoral degree (or be near completion of their doctorate) with a quantitative research orientation (e.g., business analytics, data science, machine learning, management science, statistics, econometrics, quantitative economics, or applied mathematics). When evaluating the applicants qualifications, the main focus will be on the potential to conduct high-quality scientific research in key areas relevant to the position, including Business Analytics and the potential to provide high-quality teaching.

In addition to the requirements for an assistant professor, applicants for the associate professor level are expected to have demonstrated internationally high levels of research within the scientific field of the position, high levels in teaching and contributed through institutional service and societal impact.

Applicants for full professor must demonstrate that she or he is an internationally recognised researcher with continued internationally high levels of research within the scientific field of the position. A professor is also expected to demonstrate continued high levels in teaching, institutional service and societal impact. In addition, academic leadership, experience of PhD supervision, experience and success in applying competitive research funding, international research cooperation, academic expert assignments, and experience of service within an academic department, faculty and / or university are expected.

Academic staff at Hanken are expected to carry out and supervise scientific research, provide high-quality academic teaching, closely follow the advances of their field, and participate in service to Hanken, the academic community, and society.

The full-time position has an annual working time of 1612 hours. During the academic year, it is expected that a minimum average of three days per week is spent at the office in Helsinki to actively contribute to the research and teaching environment. Teaching tasks are allocated based on the curriculum needs of the subject and by considering relevant own expertise.

Salary

The salary is based on the university salary system in Finland (includes employee healthcare as well as pension and holiday contributions). The exact salary level depends on the recruited individuals qualifications and performance. Hanken will support the selected employee with a start-up research budget, and additional research, travel and teaching development grants can also be applied for. Hanken rewards excellence in both research and teaching.

For more Information

For additional information, please contact Chair of the Department Committee, Professor Anders Löflund, anders.loflund@hanken.fi.

General instructions for applicants are provided [here](https://www.hanken.fi/en/faculty-staff/job-opportunities/job-opportunities/applications-and-selection-process). Also, read more about Hanken as an employer [here](https://www.hanken.fi/en/node/2413861).

Recruitment process and timeline

The application deadline is October 18th, 2026. Candidates will be interviewed online shortly after the application deadline. Short-listed candidates will be invited to on-site campus visits including an interview and research presentation.

How to apply

The application is to be addressed to the Rector and application materials should include:

- Cover letter in which the applicant specifies the position for which they are applying (professor, associate professor, or assistant professor)
- CV (proposed content [here](https://tenk.fi/en/advice-and-materials/template-researchers-curriculum-vitae)), including list of publications.
- Personal statement, which includes a description of past research and its scientific quality, academic impact, plans for future research and a description of the candidates service to the department and university and a description of the candidates societal impact.
- List of publications (with the most significant publications highlighted; maximum 10 for full professor applicants and maximum 5 for associate and assistant professor applicants. Applicants at the associate professor and full professor levels should additionally submit up to five publications for assessment.

jobs.title: Chef to join our international kitchen team
jobs.description:
CHEF WANTED FOR STAFF RESTAURANT IN COPENHAGEN, DENMARK

Looking for a chef position in Copenhagen with great working hours, professional cooking and weekends mostly free?

We are looking for a skilled and motivated chef to join our international kitchen team in Copenhagen, Denmark.

Your main workplace will be The Staff Restaurant at Abacus Medicine, located at Kalvebod Brygge in central Copenhagen.

This is a full-time position with working hours primarily Monday to Friday from 06:30 to 14:30 – giving you the opportunity to work in an ambitious professional kitchen while still having your afternoons, evenings and most weekends free.

Occasional evening and weekend events may occur.

THE JOB

You will become part of a professional kitchen team responsible for the daily production and service at our staff restaurant.

We cook from scratch and care about good ingredients, seasonality, flavour and proper craftsmanship.

You will work primarily with hot kitchen production and take responsibility for your own preparation and tasks while working closely with the rest of the team.

Our kitchen is busy, so we are looking for someone who works efficiently and in an organised manner without compromising quality.

Just as importantly, we are looking for a good colleague.

We believe a professional kitchen should be a place where people communicate respectfully, help each other and enjoy coming to work.

WHO ARE WE LOOKING FOR?

You may already be living in Denmark, or you may be considering moving to Copenhagen from another EU/EEA country.

We would like to hear from you if you:

  • are a trained chef or have equivalent professional kitchen experience

  • have experience from à la carte restaurants, quality staff restaurants, hotels or similar professional kitchens

  • have solid experience in the hot kitchen

  • have a genuine interest in food, ingredients and good craftsmanship

  • can organise your own work and maintain a good pace throughout the day

  • are reliable and comfortable starting work early

  • enjoy working as part of a team

  • communicate in a positive and respectful way

  • can maintain an overview when the kitchen gets busy.

A background in classic French or Mediterranean cuisine would be particularly relevant to our kitchen.

However, we are also interested in chefs who bring their own culinary background and experience. Whether your inspiration comes from France, Spain, Italy, Portugal, Greece, North or South America, Asia or somewhere else, we would like to see what you can bring to the team.

We want to taste what you are passionate about.

WHAT WE OFFER

We offer a full-time chef position in central Copenhagen with a working schedule that is unusual in the restaurant industry:

Monday–Friday
Primarily 06:30–14:30
Most evenings and weekends free

You will join a friendly and international workplace with experienced colleagues, high professional standards and room to contribute your own knowledge and ideas.

We value professional pride, teamwork, reliability and a positive working environment.

Our goal is simple: good food, good ingredients, good craftsmanship and a kitchen team that works well together.

MORE THAN A STAFF RESTAURANT

Your daily workplace will be:

The Staff Restaurant at Abacus Medicine
Kalvebod Brygge 35
1560 Copenhagen V
Denmark

Our kitchen also produces food for our small Copenhagen wine bar, Sankt Annæ 8, located in Christianshavn.

Within the same ownership group, we operate several Copenhagen restaurants, including Le Métier, La Propina and Ma Cuisine.

You will therefore become part of a wider restaurant family with different concepts and opportunities for future professional development.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION

Position: Chef
Employment: Full-time
Working hours: Primarily Monday–Friday, 06:30–14:30
Workplace: Copenhagen, Denmark
Starting date: As soon as possible / by agreement
Salary: Based on qualifications and experience and agreed individually
Evening/weekend work: Occasional events only

INTERESTED?

Send us your CV and a short application in English to:

job@willworkforfood.dk

Please write “CHEF FOR ABACUS” in the subject line.

Tell us a little about yourself, your kitchen experience, what kind of food you enjoy cooking and when you would be available to start.

Applications are reviewed continuously, and suitable candidates will be invited for an interview.

If you are currently living outside Denmark, please mention your current location and when you would potentially be available to relocate to Copenhagen.

We look forward to meeting you for a coffee and a conversation about food, ambitions and your future in Copenhagen.

The Staff Restaurant at Abacus Medicine
Copenhagen, Denmark

jobs.title: Tenure-track position in Archaeology
jobs.description:
About the position 

A tenure-track position (tenure-track in a postdoctoral position and tenured as associate professor) in Archaeology is available at The Department of Archaeology, Conservation and History (IAKH), University of Oslo. IAKH comprises the three disciplinary fields of archaeology conservation and history. The archaeology section has nine academic faculty positions, each with teaching and research components. The section’s research profile and teaching program are internationally oriented and span archaeologies of the Stone Age to the present. The announced position is focused on GIS, statistics and Mesolithic archaeology in Scandinavia.

The announced tenure-track position starts as a full-time postdoctoral position (SKO 1352) for a period of six years, including a 25 % component devoted to teaching and administrative duties. These duties include obtaining basic pedagogical qualifications. A formal midterm evaluation will be held in the fourth year of this period, and the candidate will receive feedback on performance relative to the requirements for the six-year tenure-track period. Toward the end of the six-year period, the candidate will be evaluated for a tenured position as associate professor (SKO 1011). During the final assessment, the candidate’s research performance will first be assessed by an expert (adjudication) committee within the candidate’s subject area. Subsequently, the candidate will be interviewed by an internal interview committee assessing the full range of criteria in the contract of employment.


More about the position 

Applicants apply with a research project including GIS, statistics and the Mesolithic in Scandinavia to be carried out in the initial six years period. In the application letter, candidates should also describe long term plans for building an international research group, for future development of the teaching in Stone Age Archaeology, for contributing to the public dissemination of research, and for developing their own academic career. 

The contract of employment will specify results, requirements, and criteria regarding academic production, public dissemination, research leadership and teaching that the candidate must fulfil during the six-years period to be favourably evaluated for a tenured position. According to the Regulations on appointments to tenure-track positions, with supplementary provisions for UiO, the contract of employment will also specify the criteria for the midterm and final assessment of competencies and milestones. Candidates will also be evaluated on personal suitability and ability to contribute to academic citizenship, both during the initial hiring process and during the mid-term and final evaluations. The contract of employment will further outline the Department’s obligations in supporting the candidate’s research as well as offering academic mentorship, guidance and training. 

Make sure to follow the description of required results necessary in order to be eligible for the tenured position as associate professor.


Requirements 
  • PhD or equivalent academic qualifications within archaeology of the Mesolithic in Scandinavia, with a clear profile in GIS and statistical analysis, granted within the past five years (excluding documented parental and sickness leaves) 
  • Thorough knowledge of the material culture of the Mesolithic in Scandinavia 
  • Demonstrated ability to handle large datasets, geographical information systems and theoretical perspectives on archaeological methodology/practice 
  • Experience in handling of archaeological data using high-end digital tools for quantitative and/or qualitative analysis 
  • Experience with interdisciplinary research approaches within the environmental humanities and/or crossing over to natural sciences 
  • Documented pedagogical skills (either a teaching course certificate or based on teaching experience), see how to document your pedagogical skills 
  • Documented potential for project acquisition • Interest and ability in leadership and administration 
  • Fluent oral and written communication skills in English and a Scandinavian language 
  • Personal suitability and motivation for the position 

To be eligible, candidates must have submitted for final evaluation or defended their doctoral dissertation within five years preceding the application deadline. In the former case, the appointment will be contingent upon the successful defence of the thesis. Someone who has been employed for more than one year in an ordinary postdoctoral position at the University of Oslo cannot be employed in a postdoctoral position on tenure-track terms.


In the evaluation of the applications, emphasis will be placed on:
  • The research project’s scientific merit and contribution to GIS-based and statistical approaches to the Mesolithic in Scandinavia, including the applicant’s academic and personal ability to carry out the project 
  • The applicant’s long-term plans for building and leading an international research group and successfully join in academic collaboration within and across disciplines, including plans for obtaining external research funding 
  • Academic qualifications and academic production. Originality and quality of publications will be weighted more heavily than quantity 
  • Interest in and motivation for teaching, ability to inspire and provide guidance to students, and potential to teach university-level courses about Stone Age Archaeology and within Archaeology more generally 
  • Interest and ability in leadership and administration, including collaborative skillsExperience with and potential for popular dissemination and public outreach 
  • Academic citizenship, personal suitability and potential to contribute to a positive working environment and the long-term development of teaching and research at the Department 

In the evaluation of the qualified candidates the full range of these criteria will be explicitly addressed and assessed. Academic quality, development, potential and breadth will be prioritised in this order. 

The appointed candidate should demonstrate mastery of both English and one of the Scandinavian languages as working languages.


We can offer you 
  • Exciting and meaningful tasks in an organization with an important societal mission, contributing to knowledge development, education, and enlightenment that promote sustainable, fair, and knowledge-based societal development.
  • Committed colleagues in a good working environment. 
  • Good welfare schemes.
  • Opportunity of up to 1.5 hours a week of exercise during working hours.
  • A workplace with good development and career opportunities. 
  • Membership in the Statens Pensjonskasse, which is one of Norway's best pension schemes with beneficial mortgages and good insurance schemes.
  • Salary in position as Postdoctoral Fellow, position code 1352 in salary range NOK from 595 000 to 677 000, depending on competence and experience. From the salary, 2 percent is deducted in statutory contributions to the State Pension Fund.

Read more about the benefits of working in the public sector at Employer Portal.


We need different perspectives in our work 

UiO is an open and internationally oriented comprehensive university that strives to be an inclusive and diverse workplace and academic environment. You can read more about UiO’s work on equality, inclusion, and diversity at uio.no.

We fulfill our mission most effectively when we draw upon our variety of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives. We are looking for great colleagues—could you be the next one?

We will provide appropriate accommodations should you need them. Relevant adjustments may include modifications to working hours, task adaptations, digital, technical, or physical adjustments, or other practical measures.

If you have an immigrant background, a disability, or CV gaps, we encourage you to indicate this in the job application portal. We always invite at least one qualified candidate from each group for an interview. In this context, disability is defined as an applicant who identifies as having a disability that requires workplace or employment-related accommodations. For more details about the requirements, please refer to the Employer portal (Norwegian).

The selections made in the job application portal are used for anonymized statistics that all state employers include in their annual reports.

More information about gender equality initiatives at UiO can be found here.

We hope you will apply for the position with us. 


Application

Your application must include: 

  • Application letter describing the applicant’s qualifications and motivation for the position 
  • Curriculum Vitae (including list of education, previous and current positions, teaching experience, administrative experience, and other qualifying activities) 
  • List of publications 
  • Project description (3 - 5 pages, maximum 14,000 characters. See Template for project descriptions) 
  • A realistic progress plan for all six years, including activities beyond the postdoctoral research project itself, such as teaching, professional development and project development 
  • Two writing samples (e.g. two chapters from the PhD dissertation or two academic articles) 
  • Copies of educational certificates 

Please note that all documents should be in English (or a Scandinavian language), either in the original or in translation. 

The application with attachments must be delivered in our electronic recruiting system, jobbnorge.no. Applicants with education from non-Norwegian universities must attach an explanation of their grading systems.


Selection procedure

As the first step in the evaluation process, a Selection Committee will assess all applications and invite the most qualified applicants to submit a teaching portfolio and academic works (up to 7 publications) for expert assessment. Academic texts, except for the two writing samples, shall therefore not be enclosed with the initial application. Applicants who are invited to submit academic works are asked to select three works, published within the last 5 years, to be considered as most relevant for the position. In longer publications (monographs), applicants should specify the most relevant pages. Applicants are also asked to submit a teaching portfolio of 3-6 pages documenting educational certificates, competence and experience, including a reflection note in which your own practice and learning vision is anchored in the principles of Scholarship of Teaching and Learning (SoTL). 

Finally, the most highly ranked candidates will be invited for at least one interview and trial lecture. Ranked candidates will be asked to provide a list of 3 reference persons (name, relation to candidate, e-mail and phone number). References are contacted after the interviews.


General information

Please note that we are unable to add documentation after the application deadline. As the deadline applies equally to all applicants, this policy ensures equal treatment throughout the recruitment process. If you experience difficulties uploading documents in Jobbnorge, please contact their customer service: Phone: +47 75 54 22 20 or Email: support@grade.com 

The primary method of communication throughout the process will be e-mails and messages through the recruitment system Jobbnorge. When you receive a notification of a message in Jobbnorge, please log in to read it, as it may be important.

The best qualified candidates will invited for interviews. 

Applicant lists can be published in accordance with Norwegian Freedom of Information Act § 25. When you apply for a position with us, your name will appear on the public applicant list. It is possible to request to be excluded from this list. You must justify why you want an exemption from publication and we will then decide whether we can grant your request. If we cannot, you will hear from us.

Please refer to Regulations for the Act on universities and colleges chapter 3 (Norwegian) and Guidelines concerning appointment to recruitment positions at UiO. 

The University of Oslo has a transfer agreement with all employees to secure the rights to all research results and related intellectual property.


Om arbeidsgiveren:

The University of Oslo is Norway’s oldest and highest ranked educational and research institution, with 26 500 students and 7 200 employees. With its broad range of academic disciplines and internationally recognised research communities, UiO is an important contributor to society.

The Department of archaeology, conservation and history (IAKH) is comprised of three disciplines which in different ways study the past.The department has internationally oriented archaeologists, the only conservation program in Norway and the biggest group of historians in Scandinavia. The department has close to 100 employees, including non-permanent research fellows. The study programs span archaeology from the Stone Age to the Middle Ages, object and paintings conservation, and history from Antiquity to the present age.

jobs.title: Senior Digital Design Engineer for ASIC Development
jobs.description:
Take digital ASIC designs from early concepts all the way to mass production.



We are strengthening our ASIC Design Team at Murata Finland and are looking for a Senior Digital Design Engineer to join us in Vantaa, Finland. We work in a hybrid model, so partial remote work is possible.

Murata Finland develops leading-edge gyroscope and accelerometer safety-critical sensors for global automotive, industrial and healthcare markets. We design full-custom mixed-mode ASICs from concept to volume production, including wafer-level testing.



Your role

As a Senior Digital Design Engineer, you will work on digital ASIC design from early concept development through to mass production ramp-up. You will collaborate with design partners, Murata lead engineers, product managers and the design team throughout the development process.



What you bring

We are looking for an experienced digital design professional with:

- Technical education (e.g. B.Sc., M.Sc., Ph.D. or D.Sc.) with an emphasis on digital microelectronics
- 3+ years of experience in digital design
- Experience in Verilog (or VHDL) RTL coding
- Experience in design verification using digital design tools
- Understanding of the RTL-to-GDSII flow
- A proactive, systematic and careful way of working
- Fluent communication skills in English
- Good communication skills and the ability to understand various requirements and communicate effectively with external partners and internal teams
- An innovative mindset and interest in working in an international environment



Additional experience we value

Experience in any of the following areas is considered an advantage:

- Architecture planning and functional specification
- Implementation of DSP algorithms, such as FIR or IIR filters and floating-point MAC (Multiply and Accumulate) calculations
- Digital interfaces: SPI, I2C, I3C or PSI5
- Test bench reference models using e.g. Matlab, Simulink or Python
- Verification environments: UVM (Universal Verification Methodology) based on SV (SystemVerilog) or CocoTB (Coroutine cosimulation testbench) based on Python
- ATPG (Automatic Test Pattern Generation) and LBIST (Logic Built-In Self-Test)
- FPGA, e.g. as a development environment, for customer emulator use or test support
- Digital backend design, including synthesis, timing analysis, DFT, layout and power analysis



How we work

Our culture is based on two values: employee satisfaction and customer satisfaction. Together, we have defined what these values mean in practice in what we call our cultural etiquette.

For us, employee satisfaction means helping each other, treating each other equally and in a friendly manner, and maintaining an open discussion culture. Customer satisfaction means being proactive and innovative and considering our customers needs in what we do. Would this kind of work community suit you?



Small technology, real-world impact

We believe that the tiniest things can have the greatest impact. With our innovative sensor technology, cars remain in their lanes, peoples hearts keep beating and bridges do not collapse.

In this role, you will have the opportunity to work with cutting-edge technology that contributes to the advancement of society. The combination of our Finnish and Japanese capabilities will enable safe and autonomous driving – in all places.



Interested?

For more information, please contact the hiring manager Teemu Salo tel. +358 50 327 8984 or e-mail teemu.salo@murata.com, who will be happy to tell you more about Murata and the position.

Please send your application, resume and salary expectations by 18 October 2026 via the application link. The position will be filled as soon as a suitable candidate is found.

Read more about Murata at www.muratafinland.com and follow us in LinkedIn (Murata), Instagram (@muratafinland) and Facebook (@MurataFinland).



From our News & Stories, you can read more about what it's like to work at Murata and find out if Murata is the right workplace for you! You can read about the different teams, the study and career path opportunities, as well as how development and growth appear at Murata, from product development to production work.

jobs.title: Associate Professor in Clinical Pharmacy
jobs.description:
Clinical Pharmacology, Pharmacy, and Environmental Medicine at the Department of Public Health, Faculty of Health, University of Southern Denmark, is offering a new 5-year (20%) position for an Associate Professor within clinical pharmacy. The position is to be filled from February 1st, 2027.

The academic position

The research areas of Clinical Pharmacology, Pharmacy and Environmental Medicine (CPPEM) span from pharmacological epidemiology to clinical studies and cell-based basic pharmacology. CPPEM has a strong background in investigations of exposure to environmental chemicals, pharmacoepidemiology, pharmacogenetics, pharmacokinetics, drug-drug interactions, and therapeutic drug monitoring. The academic position is affiliated with the pharmacoepidemiologic research group, that utilizes the Danish registries to assess pharmacological questions in large populations. 

The area of research is flexible within the area of pharmacoepidemiologic and clinical research and could be (but is not limited to) drug use patterns and rational pharmacotherapy. The department has a strong focus on interdisciplinary collaboration both in-house and with external researchers and the new person is expected to continue this tradition.
 

Areas of responsibility

The applicant will be expected to establish their own research area within the pharmacoepidemiologic research group at the department. Thus, the applicant should be able to attract external research funding to support research and employ scientific and technical staff. The applicant may have a background within pharmacy or medicine.

The research unit teaches in four educations: Medicine, Pharmacy, Chiropractor, and Biomedicine, and the position comes with teaching obligations within these subjects at the University as well as supervision of bachelor and master projects. Additionally, we expect that you will contribute to administrative duties, e.g., participating in Study Board or other similar activities. 

Fluent English (both written and spoken) is required. You are expected to have qualifications that renders it probable that you will be able to establish your own research area within the research unit. Further, you are required to have a PhD degree or similar research experience. 
 

Employers

Clinical Pharmacology, Pharmacy and Environmental Medicine today has approximately 50 employees. It consists of three separate research groups: pharmacoepidemiology, translational pharmacology, and environmental medicine. Additionally, it collaborates closely with the Department of Pharmacology at OUH. Collectively, this constitutes Denmark’s largest center for research, teaching and clinical service in pharmacology.

It produces approximately 100 international peer-reviewed publications per year. 

Professor Tore B. Stage heads the unit and Professor Pernille Tanggaard Andersen heads the Department.


Management

The Associate Professor answers to the research leader for the unit of Clinical Pharmacology, Pharmacy and Environmental Medicine.
 

Contact information

Further information can be obtained from the leader for the pharmacoepidemiologic research group, Professor Anton Pottegård (apottegaard@health.sdu.dk).
 

Application deadline and interviews

November 1, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. CET
 

Salary and terms of employment

The successful applicant will be employed in accordance with the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and AC (the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations).

Applications will be assessed by an expert committee. Applicants will be informed of their assessment by the university.

Applications – including the required attachments – must be sent via the below-mentioned link “Apply online". Only online applications will be accepted. Attached files must be Adobe PDF or Word format. Each field in the application form can contain up to max. 10 MB.

Only applications written in English will be accepted for evaluation.
 

Application (as pdf- or Word/docx- files):

  • a motivation letter

  • a detailed CV

  • degree certificates (inclusive of PhD diploma)

  • a complete and numbered list of publications

  • 10 scientific peer-reviewed publications considered by the candidate as most important for this position. Please notice that one pdf- or docx- file must be attached for each publication

  • a teaching portfolio detailing the candidate’s prior teaching experience, teaching skills, and teaching philosophy

  • a research plan detailing the candidate’s ideas and plans for her/his future research work

Incomplete applications regarding the above-mentioned requirements will not be assessed.

References will be obtained for the applicant who is the first choice for the position – from the applicant’s most recent employer and previous employers as required.

Further particulars concerning the application – please see the link below.
 

About SDU

The University of Southern Denmark is a world-class university driven by an ambition to promote research results that develop society. The major challenges of the 21st century are complex and multifaceted; sustainable change and solutions require new – often interdisciplinary – research-based knowledge, and the University of Southern Denmark is an indispensable stakeholder in the transition process. 

Value, quality, talented people and outstanding environments are pivotal for the University of Southern Denmark’s strategic initiatives. 

Read more: https://www.sdu.dk/en/om_sdu

The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

jobs.title: PhD scholarship at the Danish Institute for International Studies
jobs.description:
PhD scholarship at the Danish Institute for International Studies, Military Artificial Intelligence, Peace and International Security

The Danish Institute for International Studies (DIIS) is recruiting a PhD candidate to research military applications of artificial intelligence and their implications for peace and international security. We are especially interested in projects that examine how the development and use of AI-based military capabilities affect established practices of decision-making, human control, and accountability. The project should connect a nuanced understanding of the dynamics of technological change to wider questions of arms control and international regulation. 

The position is based at the DIIS Centre for Peace Research and will thematically be placed under one of the three pillars of the Centre, namely Arms control in a time of arms races and war. One of the questions that the Centre focuses on is how Nordic countries, including Denmark, can navigate a situation where the development of new technologies (e.g. AI and drones), along with increasing great power rivalry and competition in space, entail new types of security risks that traditional arms control models and treaties do not effectively regulate.

The successful candidate will develop an independent PhD project that speaks to the overall focus of the center and produces research relevant to Nordic and international debates on security and peace.

About the position 
AI is changing how military organizations collect information, assess threats, select targets and coordinate operations. These capabilities are currently developed faster than military doctrine, legal interpretation and oversight arrangements intended to govern their use. This raises questions about who exercises control, how responsibility is assigned, and how other states interpret capabilities whose operation is difficult to observe. Within this overall frame relevant proposals may examine:

  • The relationship between the adoption of AI and the development of military doctrine

  • The effects of AI-enabled decision support on military decision-making and the human role therein

  • The impact of uncertainty and opacity around the current state of AI integration among militaries on escalation dynamics and arms-race dynamics

  • Regulation of AI through multilateral governance mechanisms in and beyond the UN

  • Human judgement and accountability in military applications of AI

About DIIS and the position
The successful candidate will be employed by DIIS in a three-year, full-time PhD position, expected to commence on 1 February 2027. The candidate will be enrolled in the PhD School at the Faculty of Social Sciences at the University of Southern Denmark (SDU), while their primary place of work will be the Centre for Peace Research at DIIS.

The PhD project will be jointly supervised by a senior researcher at DIIS and Professor Ingvild Bode at SDU.

At DIIS, the PhD candidate will join an inspiring and ambitious research environment committed to advancing multidisciplinary scholarship. The successful candidate is expected to engage actively in cross-disciplinary collaboration and to value insights from colleagues working with different theoretical and methodological approaches. Such exchanges across disciplinary boundaries are central to the research environment at DIIS.

We expect the candidate to:

  • have obtained a master’s degree in a relevant field

  • have at least received the grade of 10 (or equivalent) for the master’s thesis according to the Danish 7-point grading scale and a high weighted grade point average 

  • meet the general requirements for being accepted for enrolment as a PhD candidate (see below)

  • live up to the DIIS entry criteria for PhD positions https://www.diis.dk/files/media/document/diis-entry-criteria-rev-okt-24.pdf 

  • communicate clearly in written and spoken English, and proficiency in Danish is an advantage.

DIIS as a workplace
We offer an attractive and inclusive workplace where our employees can develop. We consider knowledge sharing and feedback essential to creating a dynamic workplace. We expect you to participate proactively in the common efforts of the institute. We prioritize a high degree of presence but want our employees to have a good work-life balance. Therefore, we offer flexible working hours and some possibility of working from home. We are located very close to Copenhagen’s city center with excellent public transportation options.

DIIS is a diverse workplace, and we encourage all qualified candidates to apply for this position regardless of their personal background. DIIS is also a workplace where we consider the environmental consequences of our activities and strive to adopt more environmentally sustainable practices both in relation to our daily business at DIIS and our global travel activities.

In the assessment, consideration will be given to the following criteria:

  • The applicant has a relevant master’s degree or equivalent qualifications (corresponding to the 3 + 2 Bologna process), cf. the Danish qualifications framework for higher education

  • Quality and relevance of the project description

    • Quality and relevance of the methodical and theoretical choices

    • Consistency and coherence between the research problem and the choice of method and theory

    • The realistic and feasible scope of the PhD project

  • Relevance of the project for the DIIS Centre for Peace Research and DIIS in general

Contract and remuneration
The position as PhD candidate starts on 1 February 2027 and is a 3-year full-time position. Remuneration and other job conditions follow the general agreement between the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC) and the Danish Ministry of Finance, local collective agreements at DIIS as well as the 28 June 2019 Danish state protocol on PhD candidates. 

The standard starting salary for a PhD candidate at DIIS is 379,702,61 DKK per year excl. pensions – this may be increased depending on prior work experience after the acquisition of the master’s degree. A pension contribution of 18,07% is added to the above-mentioned salary.

Do you want to know more?
Visit http://www.diis.dk/jobs to learn more about DIIS as a workplace. Questions regarding employment and renumeration can be sent to hr@diis.dk. If you have inquiries regarding the professional focus of the position, you can contact Senior Researcher and Head of Research Unit, Mona Kanwal Sheikh at mosh@diis.dk  

The application
Deadline for applying is 23 October 2026, at 12.00 pm CET. 

Please note that we only accept applications through DIIS’ electronic recruitment system. 

Your application must include all the following documents:

  1. A motivational letter

  2. Curriculum Vitae 

  3. Master’s diploma including grades. If you hold a master’s degree which is not within the ECTS-framework, please also provide:

    • Your bachelor diploma and bachelor grades

    • A statement clarifying the subject and length (in years) of the master’s degree

    • An English translation of your diplomas 

  4. PhD project proposal (max 5 pages)

  5. Publication list

DIIS is an independent public research institution for international studies. We conduct and communicate multidisciplinary research on globalisation, security, development and foreign policy and within these areas we aim to be agenda-setting in research, policy and public debate.

DIIS participates in academic networks and publish in high-ranking academic journals, always striving to excel in academic scholarship.

We continuously assess Denmark's foreign and political situation and inform the Danish media, politicians and the public about our work

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Robot Autonomy (Planning & Navigation)
jobs.description:
Our Mission

At Laelaps AI, we believe robotics is entering a transformative decade, much like the arrival of the internet. Advances in AI, cloud computing, and hardware are reshaping what autonomous systems can do. Our mission is to build the intelligent software that powers physical security in the real world - enabling robots and sensors to handle dangerous and critical tasks that humans shouldn't have to. By engineering the orchestration layer for intelligent security, we aim to create a world that is safer, more secure, and more resilient.

We're a strong founding team based in Zurich, backed by visionary investors and advisors. We are engineering the future of security today!

THE ROLE

As a Software Engineer on Robot Autonomy, you will make our robots navigate dependably across real customer sites. Our stack works. The gap between working and dependable is the whole job. Every new site tests how a robot understands its surroundings and chooses where to go: a ramp the planner avoids, a narrow passage that exposes a poor route, a gate that changes the map, a person who steps into the robot's path, or localization drift that builds over a long patrol. You treat those cases as the real navigation problem to solve, not as edge cases.

You'll shape the technical choices behind reliable navigation, from sensor selection, ground segmentation, and traversability estimation to predicting how people and vehicles move and planning safe, efficient routes around them. The system has to work day and night, in challenging weather, across different embodiments and changing site conditions. We measure success by whether the robot completes its patrol on a live site, not by how it performs in simulation.

WHAT YOU'LL WORK ON

  • Navigation and path-planning design: how robots represent traversable space, select routes, avoid obstacles, and reach goals across complex sites.

  • Sensor integration driven by navigation requirements, including what ground segmentation and traversability estimation need in day, night, and challenging weather.

  • Environment understanding: how the robot distinguishes ground from obstacles and estimates which terrain is safe and practical to traverse.

  • Behavior prediction: anticipate how people, vehicles, and other dynamic obstacles will move, and plan routes that stay safe and efficient around them.

  • Field reliability: reproduce failures from deployments, find the root cause, and fix it at the right layer, from sensor data and maps to costmaps, planners, and recovery behaviors.

  • Planning under imperfect localization: plans that stay useful when the state estimate drifts and the robot must execute routes in tight or dynamic environments, working with the rest of Robot Autonomy on localization and control.

  • Validation on real robots: logs, simulation, and repeatable field tests to verify that design choices and changes hold across routes, lighting, weather, and site layouts.

  • New autonomy capabilities: work with the engineers building the operator application and backend so operator requests and new robot capabilities rest on a sound navigation design.

  • The field feedback loop: work closely with forward-deployed engineers to turn site issues into bugs, design changes, and improvements to the navigation stack.

  • Regular site visits to build a practical understanding of how robots and sensors behave in real operating conditions.

WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR

We're looking for an engineer who has taken a robotics system from unreliable to dependable and takes ownership beyond individual tickets. You can explain why you made a navigation design choice and what it costs. When a robot takes a bad route, you can tell whether the planner, the map, the state estimate, or the robot's behavior is at fault, and you fix the right one. You are comfortable in the field and want to understand how robots behave in real customer environments.

YOUR BACKGROUND:

  • A Master's degree or PhD in mechanical engineering, computer science, robotics, electrical engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

  • Proven track record building and deploying navigation on ground mobile robots in the real world (3+ years or equivalent depth).

  • Hands-on experience with mobile robot navigation and path planning: route or local planning, static and dynamic obstacle avoidance, costmaps, or recovery behaviors.

  • Understanding of how mapping and localization affect navigation, and the ability to diagnose when a planning issue is actually caused by the map, the state estimate, or robot behavior.

  • Understanding of how lighting, weather, terrain, and sensor limitations affect perception and navigation, with experience developing or validating systems for demanding real-world conditions.

  • Hands-on experience with robotics sensors and hardware, especially LiDAR, IMUs, and cameras. You can investigate issues across software, networking, and hardware boundaries.

  • Experience testing and debugging navigation on physical robots using logs, visualization, simulation, and repeatable field tests.

  • Strong ROS 2, C++, and Python skills.

  • Clear communication of navigation and path-planning design choices and their trade-offs.

  • Willingness to visit customer sites regularly.

NICE TO HAVE:

  • Experience with legged robots or with more than one robot embodiment.

  • Experience with Nav2 or a comparable navigation framework.

  • Motion prediction or planning among people and vehicles, such as trajectory forecasting or socially aware navigation.

  • Terrain mapping and traversability methods: elevation mapping, learned traversability, or semantic segmentation for navigation.

  • Experience with night-time or all-weather sensing, such as thermal cameras or LiDAR in rain and fog.

  • Background in security, defence, or other safety-critical robotics deployments.

What We Offer

  • Ownership: you are able to ship products and deliver project end-to-end.

  • Mission: autonomous security that keeps people and critical sites safe, including in defence.

  • Career path: a ground-floor seat with real runway. Prove your value and you will not have barriers to grow.

  • Team: work directly with PhD-level co-founders in AI, Robotics, and Physics, alongside a strong (and fun) founding team.

  • Compensation: Competitive equity/salary package

  • Culture: International founding team that is serious about building but does not take itself too seriously.

THE ROLE

As a Software Engineer on Robot Autonomy, you will build and own the state estimation that tells our robots how they are moving and where they are. You'll fuse data from IMUs, cameras, LiDAR, GNSS, and platform-specific odometry into accurate, real-time estimates that support reliable autonomy day and night, across different robot platforms.

This is a builder's role first: you'll use the estimation methods and tools best suited to the problem, then do the engineering needed to make them work on real robots. Our robots operate in complex environments where terrain, weather, vibration, lighting, and sensor dropouts degrade measurements. We care less about novelty for its own sake and more about whether your systems perform reliably across platforms in the field.

WHAT YOU'LL WORK ON

  • Design and ship real-time estimators for position, orientation, velocity, and angular velocity across our robot platforms.

  • Fuse data from multiple sensors, handling noise, asynchronous measurements, calibration errors, changing sensor quality, and dropouts.

  • Develop estimation approaches suited to different platforms, including reusable components and interfaces that account for their distinct sensors and dynamics.

  • Improve localization and odometry in challenging conditions, including GNSS-denied environments and cases with degraded or intermittent sensing.

  • Integrate state estimation with perception, planning, and control so downstream systems receive reliable estimates and useful uncertainty information.

  • Investigate failures using logs, datasets, simulation, and field testing; identify root causes and verify that fixes improve performance on real robots.

  • Build evaluation and testing workflows that make estimator performance measurable and repeatable across robot types and operating conditions.

  • Work closely with the rest of Robot Autonomy and with forward-deployed engineers to turn deployment experience into improvements to the estimation stack.

WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR

We're looking for an engineer who has built or deployed state estimation systems for real robotic or autonomous platforms. You understand that estimator performance depends on the whole system: sensor behavior, calibration, timing, platform dynamics, and how autonomy uses the estimate.

You're comfortable choosing an approach based on the operational need, then making it robust through careful implementation, evaluation, and field validation. You measure success by whether robots operate reliably in the real world, not by algorithmic novelty alone.

YOUR BACKGROUND:

  • A Master's degree or PhD in mechanical engineering, computer science, robotics, electrical engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

  • Proven experience building or deploying state estimation, localization, or odometry systems for robots or autonomous systems (3+ years or equivalent depth).

  • Strong understanding of nonlinear state estimation, sensor fusion, Kalman filtering, and uncertainty representation.

  • Experience working with real sensor data and practical issues such as noise, calibration, synchronization, vibration, and data loss.

  • Strong C++ and Python skills, with experience building robotics software in ROS 2.

  • Ability to analyze estimation failures and debug issues across sensors, software, and robot behavior.

  • Experience evaluating robotics systems using recorded data, simulation, or physical robots.

  • Strong software engineering practices, including version control, reproducible experiments, and disciplined performance evaluation.

NICE TO HAVE:

  • Experience with both ground and aerial robots, or with applying estimation methods across different robot platforms.

  • Experience with visual-inertial odometry, LiDAR-inertial odometry, SLAM, or GNSS/INS integration.

  • Familiarity with optimization-based estimation and factor graph tools such as GTSAM or Ceres.

  • Understanding of robot dynamics and how estimation affects planning and control.

  • Experience operating robots in challenging conditions such as GNSS-denied areas, low light, dust, rain, or high vibration.

  • Experience monitoring or improving deployed robotics systems in the field.

jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff - Device Software Engineer
jobs.description:
Technology that speaks your language

Domera Labs builds Ami, the first AI companion for seniors. Ami brings the power of a smartphone into a more human form: voice-first and deeply personalized

We at Domera Labs are rethinking human-machine interaction from first principles by introducing a better interface to interact with technology: voice

By combining the most intuitive hardware design with frontier AI, Ami makes AI accessible for the fastest growing demographic worldwide. The goal is to make the everyday life older adults more seamless, while addressing that generation's biggest challenge: loneliness and isolation. With Ami we are building the category leader of a new hardware paradigm by building a full standalone device (and not a gadget) that aims to makes the smartphones of today redundant.

The underlying technology of Ami combines a model-agnostic streaming pipeline consisting of proprietary models and off-the-shelf frontier models to create a hyper-personalized and proactive user experience. The backbone of Ami is built by our foundational lab that builds a social intelligence model that is optimized for social interaction, human behavior and interpersonal skills.

Domera Labs has secured large distribution agreements, a model co-development partnership with a leading AI lab, and ODM manufacturing proposals. We are looking for people who want to build at the intersection of human-machine interaction, mass-consumer facing hardware and shape frontier research with social/non-quantifiable benchmarking.


Core Responsibilities

You own the software that makes Ami work. Your primary responsibility is to architect, write and ship the on-device application and services for our mass-market consumer device, from voice interaction and cloud connectivity to onboarding, recovery and everyday reliability. You will work directly with our ODM and silicon partners to integrate that software with the underlying platform.

Our target hardware uses a Qualcomm SoC with Android/AOSP or embedded Linux depending on the final platform selection.

Our users are 75 years old and there is no screen, no settings menu, and no IT support. If the device does not work out of the box, it fails. Your job is to make the following work.

  • On-device application: build and own Ami's application and services, including interaction logic, real-time audio streaming, cloud communication, local state and recovery from network interruptions or service failures

  • Device identity and fleet management: provisioning, unique device identity, secure key storage, and the systems that let us know what every unit in the field is doing

  • The maintenance channel: a reliable service and diagnostics path to the device (BLE, USB-C, or both) for field debugging, factory test, and recovery

  • Out-of-the-box experience: first-boot network onboarding that a senior can complete alone, with no screen and no smartphone as a crutch. This is the single highest-stakes piece of the product

  • Flash and update management: partition layout, A/B OTA with rollback, staged fleet rollouts, and bricking as a category of bug that never happens

  • Base platform behaviors: boot and recovery, factory and soft resets, button and LED mappings, audio feedback, power states and battery behavior

  • The audio front end: working with our ODM and silicon partners on mic array, echo cancellation, wake word, and the latency budget from mic to first spoken token

  • Bringing the device through EVT, DVT, and PVT with our ODM as the technical counterpart on our side

 

What we are looking for

  • ⁠A builder's mindset: ship > fail > learn > improve

  • Stay focused when multiple priorities compete and the ranking is unclear

  • Work seamlessly across research and engineering

  • Can navigate ambiguity and make progress in fast-moving research environments

  • This is a founding-level position. You will work directly with the founders, shape the architecture from the ground up, and see your work in users' hands within months, not years.

 

Technical Requirements

  • You have shipped a connected consumer device to production, not just to a demo table. You know what goes wrong between DVT and mass production

  • Strong hands-on experience building production device applications and services on Android/AOSP, using Kotlin or Java and C/C++ for native components and hardware integration. You can own the on-device application end to end, including background execution, connectivity, audio and integration with platform services. Experience with embedded Linux is a plus; Python proficiency for tooling and testing is expected.

  • Experience developing for AOSP-based devices beyond standard smartphone apps: integrating privileged applications and services, working with system permissions and hardware interfaces, and collaborating with an ODM or silicon vendor on the underlying platform. Qualcomm platform experience is a plus.

  • Wireless connectivity in the real world: Wi-Fi provisioning, BLE, and ideally cellular. You have debugged a device that would not join a network in someone's home

  • OTA and flash: bootloaders, secure boot, A/B partitioning, rollback, and staged rollouts across a fleet

  • You can diagnose issues across application code, platform services and hardware interfaces

  • A builder's mindset: you'd rather ship and measure than debate

  • Bonus: real-time audio pipelines (I2S, DSP, AEC, wake word), on-device ML inference, factory test and manufacturing line bring-up, regulatory certification (CE, FCC), power optimization for battery life, experience in NLU / NLP

 

We lean toward senior engineers who can independently own production device software, but demonstrated ownership matters more than years of experience. Experience integrating real-time AI services into a consumer product is a plus.

Etsimme vakinaiseen työsuhteeseen mielenterveys, päihde- ja asunnottomuustyöstä kiinnostunutta sosiaaliohjaajaa Alppikadun asumispalveluyksikköön.

Sosiaaliohjaajat ovat asiakkaiden tukena asumisen eri vaiheissa. Tehtävä sisältää mm. vuokranmaksun seurantaa, etuuksien hakemista yhdessä asiakkaan kanssa, tuen tarpeen arviointia sekä yhteistyötä eri verkostojen kanssa. Tehtävässä korostuu eri tavoin asumisen sujumisen ja jatkumisen turvaaminen. Työ on arkisin tapahtuvaa päivätyötä liukuvalla työajalla ja saat suunnitella työpäiväsi kulun itse.

Sosiaaliohjaajien työryhmä koostuu neljästä sosiaaliohjaajasta, joista kukin toimii noin 20 asukkaan omana sosiaaliohjaajana. Työn tukena ovat yksikön ohjaajat, sairaanhoitaja, työvalmentaja, tiiminvetäjä, esihenkilö ja yksikön johtaja.

Olet koulutukseltasi sosionomi ja sinulla voi olla aiempaa kokemusta päihde- ja mielenterveystyöstä, mutta tärkeintä on kyky kohdata asiakkaat vaihtelevissa elämäntilanteissaan ja toimia osana moniammatillista työyhteisöä. Omaat hyvän huumorintajun, paineen sietokykyä ja kestät keskeneräisyyttä. Tarjoamme vaihtelevan ja mielenkiintoisen työn, jossa kahta samanlaista päivää ei ole. Saat kattavan perehdytyksen ja osaavan työyhteisön tuen työllesi.

Alppikadun asumispalveluyksikkö toimii Asunto ensin -periaatteen mukaisesti tarjoten tuettua asumista asunnottomuutta kokeneille. Yksikössä on 89 asukaspaikkaa ja henkilökunta paikalla ympäri vuorokauden. Yksikön perustehtävänä on turvata asukkaisen asuminen omissa vuokra-asunnoissaan. Kantavana ajatuksena on tarjota asukkaille mahdollisuus ihmisarvoiseen elämään, johon olennaisena osana kuuluu asunto, osallisuuden kokemus omaan elämään, yhteisöön ja yhteiskuntaan.

jobs.title: Santa Claus
jobs.description:
SANTA CLAUS WANTED IN ROVANIEMI CITY CENTRE – JOIN SANTA CLAUS CITY OFFICE!

Would you like to bring joy and create unforgettable moments as Santa Claus? Santa Claus City Office is looking for a Santa Claus performer at Lordi Square in the heart of Rovaniemi for the season from 1 November 2026 to 31 March 2027.

SHIFTS AND EARNING OPPORTUNITIES Evening shifts are available every day from 4 pm to 9 pm or 10 pm. Morning shifts are also available on Saturdays and Sundays.

Ideally, we would like to find someone who can work plenty of shifts. For the right person, we offer good pay and the opportunity to make this a full-time job for the season.

However, shifts can also be shared among several Santa performers as a team, just as we did last year. You do not need to be available for every shift – a few shifts a week or occasional cover would also be a valuable help. You can combine this role with another job and start with a few shifts to get to know the work.

Please feel free to apply and tell us what availability would suit you. Lets see how we can arrange the shifts together!

WHAT IS THE WORK LIKE? Being Santa is all about warm welcomes and creating happy moments. You will meet children and adults from around the world, chat with them and become part of their Christmas memories.

This is a cheerful, people-focused role where you can bring your own personality and sense of humour. We value a relaxed, positive atmosphere where both our team and our visitors feel welcome.

WHO ARE WE LOOKING FOR? We are looking for a warm, calm and friendly person with a customer service mindset who feels comfortable stepping into the role of Santa Claus. We value a convincing Santa presence, life experience and the ability to connect with both children and adults.

Basic conversational English is enough – you do not need perfect grammar or fluent English. Most of our visitors are not native English speakers either, so basic English and a willingness to chat will take you a long way. Any additional language skills are a bonus!

International and English-speaking applicants are warmly welcome. Previous experience is not essential, as we provide training. Training will begin soon, and we will agree on your starting date with you.

LOCATION Santa Claus City Office, Lordi Square, Rovaniemi, Finland. You will work in a warm Santas cabin brought to the square for the season.

HOW TO APPLY Send us a short introduction about yourself by email. Tell us why you would suit the role of Santa Claus, how much work you are looking for and when you could start training. Please also describe your language skills and your availability for evening shifts and weekend morning and evening shifts.

We would love to hear from you!

CONTACT

Marko Paksuniemi, Santa Claus City Office

paksuniemimarko@yahoo.com

EMAIL SUBJECT JOB APPLICATION – Santa Claus / Santa Claus City Office

PLEASE NOTE BEFORE APPLYING Unfortunately, we are unable to provide accommodation. Applicants must already be in Rovaniemi or be able to arrange their own travel to Rovaniemi and accommodation for the entire employment period. Applicants must also have the legal right to work in Finland.

jobs.employer: Speciallæge i øre-, næse- og halssygdomme v/ Gitte Obel
jobs.description:
Kompetent lægesekretær eller klinikassistent søges til velfungerende speciallægepraksis i øre- næse- halssygdomme.

 

Øre-næse-halsklinikken i Vejen er en speciallægeklinik med én fast speciallæge og én

konsultationssygeplejerske samt én lægesekretær. Vores dygtige sekretær søger nye udfordringer, hvorfor vi søger en ny medarbejder til et alsidigt og spændende job.

 

Om jobbet

Vi søger en dygtig,  engageret og arbejdsom medarbejder. Arbejdet foregår i tæt samarbejde med sygeplejersken og speciallægen. Vi har godt humør i hverdagen. Antallet af timer kan aftales fra 25-30 timer fordelt på 4-5 hverdage.

Arbejdsdagen består blandt andet af visitering af patienter i telefontiden som er ca. 2-3 timer dagligt. Desuden er der flere afvekslende opgaver såsom høreprøver, allergitest, lungefunktionsundersøgelse, svimmelhedsundersøgelser samt rengøring af instrumenter. Du vil blive grundigt oplært i alle opgaver. Der er desuden operationsdage i fuld bedøvelse, hvor du skal hjælpe til.

 

Om dig

Vi forventer en god arbejdsmoral med glæde og godt humør til patienterne. Det er vigtigt med gode kommunikative egenskaber og imødekommenhed. Du har gåpåmod, er sympatisk og pligtopfyldende.

Det er vigtigt, at du er robust og kan håndtere en til tider travl hverdag i klinikken.

Vi forestiller os, at du har en uddannelse som enten lægesekretær eller klinikassistent, men hvis du passer ind i vores team og har den rette indstilling, er uddannelsen mindre vigtig.

 

Om os

Vi tilbyder en fantastisk arbejdsplads med en varieret arbejdsdag, gode kolleger og supervision. Vi sætter patientens velvære i klinikken højt og bidrager med godt humør. Faglighed og ordentlighed er i højsæde.

 

Løn efter overenskomst og individuel aftale

Ansættelse: pr. 01.11.2026 eller efter aftale.

jobs.title: Postdoc in intestinal regeneration and mucosal immunology
jobs.description:
A full-time (100%) postdoctoral position is available in the lab of Dr. Srustidhar Das, at the Department of Clinical Research and at the Research Unit of Inflammation Research, Department of Molecular Medicine, Faculty of Health Sciences, University of Southern Denmark. The position is limited to two years, with the possibility of extension subject to funding.

Research tasks

The position comprises research, teaching, professional development and supervision within intestinal tissue regeneration, epithelial biology, mucosal immunology and inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). The postdoc will join a translational research programme that investigates how inflammation reshapes the intestinal epithelium and its surrounding tissue niche, and how these changes can be targeted to promote safe and durable mucosal healing.

The successful candidate will combine patient-derived organoid and co-culture models with molecular biology, functional assays, and computational analysis of single-cell and spatial datasets. The position is particularly suited to a researcher who can connect experimental biology with bioinformatics and clinically relevant questions.

Research environment

The postdoc will be embedded in a dynamic and highly collaborative research environment spanning the Department of Clinical Research and the Department of Molecular Medicine at SDU. The project benefits from close interaction among basic scientists, clinicians, bioinformaticians and translational researchers, with strong links to Odense University Hospital and access to patient-derived material, advanced disease models and state-of-the-art molecular technologies.

The environment provides excellent opportunities to develop an independent research profile, contribute to clinically relevant discoveries in IBD and tissue regeneration, and build collaborations across experimental, computational and clinical disciplines.

Research project

The project investigates how inflammatory history establishes persistent epithelial and niche memory, shapes epithelial plasticity and influences intestinal regeneration in IBD. Using patient-derived biopsies, intestinal organoids, fibroblasts and immune-cell co-cultures, we will determine how epithelial memory and injury-induced cell-state transitions influence regenerative capacity and distinguish effective from impaired mucosal healing.

Functional experiments will be integrated with single-cell RNA sequencing, chromatin-accessibility analysis, spatial transcriptomics and spatial epigenomics. CRISPR-engineered patient-derived organoids, including lineage reporters and targeted genetic perturbations, will be used to trace epithelial cell states and validate candidate mechanisms. Selected organoids will also be tested in engraftment models to determine whether regenerative phenotypes translate into improved tissue integration and repair in vivo.

Key responsibilities

  • Establish and manipulate patient-derived intestinal organoids and fibroblast–immune-cell co-cultures to investigate epithelial plasticity, cell-state transitions, regeneration, inflammatory responses and barrier function.

  • Generate and validate CRISPR-engineered organoids, including reporter lines and targeted genetic perturbations, and perform engraftment studies to assess regenerative potential in vivo.

  • Analyse and integrate scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq, spatial transcriptomic and spatial epigenomic datasets using reproducible workflows for quality control, differential analysis, cell-state annotation, trajectory analysis and multimodal integration.

  • Apply molecular and cellular methods, including qPCR, immunostaining, advanced microscopy, flow cytometry and ELISA-based assays, and validate candidate pathways using pharmacological and CRISPR-based perturbations where appropriate.

  • Collaborate with clinicians, experimental scientists and bioinformaticians to analyse and interpret patient-derived samples and data.

  • Maintain accurate and reproducible records, present findings, prepare manuscripts and conference contributions, and contribute to grant applications, teaching and supervision where relevant.

Expectations of qualifications

The successful applicant must hold a PhD in molecular biology, cell biology, immunology, bioinformatics, computational biology, regenerative medicine, biomedicine or a closely related discipline, with documented research experience relevant to the project.

Essential qualifications

  • Documented experience in organoid biology, preferably involving intestinal or other tissue-derived epithelial organoids, and in designing mechanistic studies of epithelial plasticity and regeneration.

  • A strong background in tissue regeneration, epithelial biology, mucosal immunology, inflammatory disease or a closely related field.

  • Demonstrated expertise in analysing single-cell or spatial-omics data, with proficiency in R and/or Python and experience developing reproducible computational workflows.

  • Hands-on experience in molecular and cell biology, with the ability to design, perform, troubleshoot and interpret experiments using a structured and careful approach to data analysis, documentation and responsible research practice.

  • A strong publication record appropriate to career stage; excellent written and spoken English; and the ability to drive projects independently while collaborating effectively in a multidisciplinary and international environment.

Desirable qualifications

  • Experience with intestinal organoids, patient-derived material, fibroblast or immune-cell culture, or epithelial–stromal–immune co-culture models.

  • Experience integrating scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq, spatial transcriptomic, spatial epigenomic or other multimodal datasets.

  • Familiarity with advanced imaging, quantitative image analysis, flow cytometry, organoid phenotyping or high-content screening.

  • Demonstrated experience generating and validating CRISPR-engineered organoids, including knock-in reporters or targeted gene perturbations, and with intestinal organoid engraftment or transplantation and in vivo assessment of epithelial regeneration is highly preferred.

  • An interest in supervising junior researchers and contributing to collaborative teaching and research activities.

Research strategy for OUH and the Department of Clinical Research

The joint research strategy for the Department of Clinical Research and Odense University Hospital sets the direction for our shared research efforts in the years ahead. Rooted in the vision –We conduct research together to shape the patient care of the future – it focuses in particular on: cross-disciplinary research – with people at the centre; strong research environments – as drivers of development; and the research journey – from idea to impact. Further information on the joint research strategy of the Department of Clinical Research and Odense University Hospital is available here.

Further information 

For further information, please contact Dr. Srustidhar Das, Department of Clinical Research and Department of Molecular Medicine, University of Southern Denmark (SDU), tel.: +45 71504339, e-mail: srudas@health.sdu.dk

Application deadline

November 1, 2026 at 23.59 hrs. (CET).

Salary and terms of employment

The applicant will be employed in accordance with the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and AC (the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations).

The position as Postdoc is placed within salary steps 4–8 of the Danish state salary scale, depending on seniority. In addition, a centrally agreed postdoc allowance is paid, and further qualification- and function-related allowances may be negotiated.

The work location will be at Campusvej 55, 5230 Odense M, Denmark.

Application

Applications must be submitted electronically using the link “Apply now” - see below.

We strongly recommend that you read How to apply for a position at SDU before you apply.

Only applications written in English will be accepted for evaluation.

The application must include (as PDF files) (please note that the application (the motivation letter) and CV must not exceed 10 MB in total):

  • a motivation letter

  • a detailed CV

  • degree certificates (inclusive of Ph.D.-diploma)

  • a complete and numbered list of publications

  • 3 scientific peer-reviewed publications considered by the candidate as most important for this position. Please note that a copy of each publication must be attached as a pdf file.

    • It is permitted to merge copies of the selected publications into a single PDF file.

  • a teaching portfolio detailing the candidate’s prior teaching experience, teaching skills, and teaching philosophy

  • a detailed description of research experience

  • an explanation of other qualifications relevant to the position

For technical issues, please contact: hcm-support@sdu.dk

Please note that all the above-mentioned information must be included in the application.  

Applications received after the deadline and/or incomplete applications will not be considered.

Assessment

Shortlisting will be used as part of the initial selection process. 

Assessment of shortlisted applications will be done under the existing Appointment Order for universities. Shortlisted applications will be assessed by an assessment committee. The committee may request additional information, and, if so, it is the responsibility of the applicant to provide the necessary material. 

When the assessment committee has submitted its report, the applicants will receive part of the evaluation that concerns themselves. 

References will be obtained for the preferred candidate from their current and previous employers. Applicants invited for interview should expect to complete a work-related personality assessment.

Living and working in Denmark

- Follow all health, safety, and hygiene procedures to provide a safe environment for guests and team members.

- Respond to guest requests professionally and efficiently to help create a memorable stay.

- Support the housekeeping team by working collaboratively to achieve daily room and cleanliness targets.

- A passion for spreading the light and warmth of hospitality.

- Acting with integrity and always doing the right thing.

- A positive and team-oriented attitude.

- Attention to detail and pride in maintaining high cleanliness standards.

- Reliability, flexibility, and a strong work ethic.

- A sense of ownership and accountability for your work.

- A focus on delivering exceptional experiences for every guest, every day.


**Previous housekeeping or cleaning experience is an advantage, but a positive attitude and willingness to learn are even more important.**

Customer service is a central part of the role, and success requires a customer-oriented mindset and strong interpersonal skills. In this position, you will have a direct impact on customer experience and the smooth running of customer relationships. Therefore, active collaboration, clear communication, and a solution-oriented approach are essential.

Every employee is important to us. We treat everyone equally and with respect and do not tolerate discrimination in any form. We operate responsibly and are committed to maintaining a safe and healthy work community.

People enjoy working at N-Clean, and our employee eNPS score is an outstanding 55! This is reflected in our daily work through mutual respect and a genuine commitment to succeeding together.

Lieksan Sataman Grillitupa – Lieksa, Finland

Lieksan Sataman Grillitupa is a small restaurant located in Lieksa, Finland. We serve Chinese food as well as hamburgers, French fries and other grill and fast-food products.

We are looking for a Chinese Cuisine Cook / Restaurant Worker for a full-time, permanent employment relationship.

Job description

This is a versatile restaurant position. The main responsibility is preparing Chinese food, but the employee will also participate in the restaurants other daily operations.

The duties include:

\* preparing Chinese dishes

\* handling, cutting and preparing ingredients

\* preparing cold dishes and hot dishes

\* independently preparing food for larger groups of customers

\* designing and developing approximately 4–5 new Chinese dishes every year

\* developing the Chinese menu together with the employer

\* preparing hamburgers, French fries and other grill and fast-food products

\* cashier duties and customer service

\* washing dishes

\* cleaning and maintaining the kitchen and restaurant

\* arranging and restocking ingredients and other products

\* other daily duties required in a small restaurant

The position is not limited to Chinese cooking. The employee is expected to work flexibly in different areas of the restaurant, including the kitchen, cashier, customer service and cleaning.

What we expect from you

\* experience in Chinese cooking

\* ability to independently prepare Chinese dishes from preparation to finished food

\* good practical skills in handling ingredients, preparation and cooking

\* ability to prepare food for larger groups of customers

\* interest in designing and developing new Chinese dishes

\* careful, responsible and motivated approach to work

\* good hygiene and food safety practices

\* flexibility and willingness to perform different restaurant duties

\* good teamwork skills

Previous professional experience in restaurant or kitchen work is an advantage.

Employment conditions

\* Employment type: Permanent / open-ended

\* Working time: Full-time, according to the applicable collective agreement

\* Expected starting date: February 2027

Annual restaurant closure

The employment relationship continues during the annual closure. Arrangements during the closure period, including any temporary layoff arrangements, will be made in accordance with Finnish legislation and the applicable MaRa–PAM collective agreement.
